screening_results.reason: Study uses task-based BOLD fMRI of social stimuli (affiliation, isolation) and explicit social-cognition task (pleasantness ratings), satisfying I3. The sample includes a healthy adult group with mean age 20.75 (n=32 reported with separate older and younger group statistics), satisfying I4 (healthy adults aged 18–65 are included and reported). The analyses were fit over the whole brain and report group-level, voxelwise contrasts with reported peak coordinates (conjunctions and between-group contrasts), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and include within-group whole-brain task effects rather than only between-group contrasts. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

The study reports task-based fMRI during social-motivation tasks (power and affiliation film clips), satisfying social-related task criterion. Participants are healthy adults (n=17, mean age 23.6) meeting the sample criterion. The NeuroStore record indicates whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference for group-level, voxelwise contrasts (power-related clips > control; affiliation-related clips > control) and cross-subject regressions, with reported peak coordinates—fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. Results are reported as peaks/tables. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study uses fMRI during a clearly social-related task (social vs solitary sentence generation/reading during encoding and subsequent recognition), meeting I3. The sample is healthy adults (n=24, age range 18–28), meeting I4. The record reports group-level whole-brain task contrasts: Analyses 21600991_analysis_4 and _5 indicate model fit and inference over the whole brain with cluster-level thresholding (p<0.001) and reported peaks (Table t0015), satisfying I5 (and acceptable reporting per I6). Both ROI and whole-brain results are present; no exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical fMRI data). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It uses task-based fMRI during a social cognition paradigm (observing social vs individual actions; gaze manipulation) (I3). The sample is healthy adults (n=17, mean age 26) (I4). The report contains group-level, whole-brain voxelwise within-group contrasts (main effects of action type and gaze, and an interaction), with thresholding at voxel-level (p<0.001, cluster extent) and reported peak coordinates (Table 1), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) apply. Therefore the study should be included.

The NeuroStore record reports an fMRI task examining social interaction (gaze and facial expressions) in healthy adults (mean age 25.9). Group-level, whole-brain analyses were performed (model fit over whole brain; second-level one-sample t-tests) and coordinates/peaks are reported in tables for multiple within-group contrasts (e.g., SOC>ARB, ME>OTHER). Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 18–65), I5 (whole-brain, group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported as coordinate tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Note: minor inconsistency in participant sex counts in the record does not affect eligibility.

The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (observing and judging others' regret), includes a healthy adult sample (n=24, ages within 18–65), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (second-level whole-brain model fit with reported peak coordinates and cluster thresholds). Whole-brain results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy group. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study examines social communicative intentions (social communication) using an event-related prosody categorization task, meeting the review topic. Participants are healthy adults (n=22, mean age 27.35) satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain within-group task contrasts (Clear > Ambiguous and Ambiguous > Clear) with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference, thresholded and reported as MNI coordinates (reported peaks), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Coordinate tables and reported peaks are present. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity-only, and not between-group-only. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

Exclusion E2 met: the reported inference is restricted to a region-of-interest with FWE small-volume correction (SVC). Although the model was fit over the whole brain, the paper reports significance only within an ROI (SVC), and does not provide an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map for the healthy group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task engages affiliative emotion/social-related processing) and I4 (healthy adult participants, n=12, age mean 23.8). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain, voxelwise healthy-group task-evoked statistical map reported; results are ROI-restricted). Full text appears complete in this record.

The study reports event-related fMRI during a social-related task (face target detection), satisfying I3. The sample is a healthy adult group (n=19; ages 19.3–47.5), satisfying I4. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported (model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain) with peak coordinates/tables for within-group contrasts including Face Targets > Novels, satisfying I5; reporting in tables meets I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are triggered. Therefore the paper meets all required inclusion criteria for the review.

The paper reports task-based fMRI during clearly social interactions (live face-to-face interaction and joint attention tasks), satisfying I3. Samples are healthy adults with ages 18–29 and separate analyses reported for these groups (n=16 and n=13), satisfying I4. Multiple group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts are reported with whole-brain inference and peak coordinate tables (e.g., Live>Recorded, JA>SA), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity/resting-state-only (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E4), ages are within 18–65 (E5), and this is empirical fMRI data (not a review/methods-only) (E6).

The study uses fMRI during social cognition tasks (I3) and includes a healthy adult control group reported separately (I4). However, the NeuroStore record shows only between-group whole-brain contrasts (HC > BPD, BPD > HC), ROI-based contrasts, and group×task interactions; no unmasked, whole-brain, group-level healthy-control task activation map (within-group or main effect for the healthy group) is reported. This fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Therefore the study is excluded.

The study uses task-based fMRI of social cognition (watching social scenes; contrasts of emotional vs. neutral and two-person vs. one-person). Participants are healthy adults (n=16; mean age 27.8), satisfying the sample criterion. Crucially, the NeuroStore record reports group-level, whole-brain within-group task contrasts with whole-brain inference (e.g., Emotional>Neutral and Social relation>single person: model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain; FDR q<0.05; peaks reported in Table 1), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy group. Results are reported as coordinate peaks in tables (acceptable per I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical). Therefore include.

I3 and I4 are met: the study used task-based fMRI (Gaze Perception / Joint Attention Task) in a healthy adult sample (n=24, ages 20–34). However, I5 is NOT met: although models were fit over the whole brain, all reported statistical inference was explicitly restricted to regions-of-interest with FWE small-volume correction (ROI/SVC). The document does not report any unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation maps for the healthy group. Therefore the study reports only ROI-based inferential results and meets exclusion criterion E2. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E2.

The NeuroStore record describes an fMRI study of moral emotions in healthy adults (n=13, mean age 25.5) using whole-brain modeling, but the only reported statistical maps in the extraction are sex-comparison contrasts (Females > Males; Males > Females). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social/moral task) and I4 (healthy adult sample). Inclusion criterion I5 is not met because the document does not report any unmasked, group-level whole-brain task-evoked map (e.g., main effect of condition or within-group condition contrasts) for the healthy group; instead only between-sex contrasts are listed. This triggers exclusion E4 (studies that report only between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Therefore the study is excluded.

The study uses fMRI during a social-emotional task (I3) and reports a healthy adult group (n=29, mean age 32.4) (I4). However, it does not report any group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group (I5 not met). All healthy-group task contrasts are reported with model fit and inference restricted to a region-of-interest; the only whole-brain analysis in the record is a cross-subject regression reported within the patient (rMDD) group, not an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect. Therefore the paper fails the required whole-brain healthy-group criterion and must be excluded.

The study examines facial emotion processing with fMRI during a social-related task (perceptual judgment of faces), satisfying I3. The sample includes healthy adult participants alongside Asperger patients, satisfying I4. However, although whole-brain analyses were performed, the document only reports within-group whole-brain task maps for the patient/AS group (n=9). Results for healthy controls are not reported as an unmasked, whole-brain within-group activation map; only between-group contrasts (controls > AS and omnibus group×intensity interactions) are provided. Therefore the paper does not provide the required healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map (I5 not met) and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group effects without a healthy-group whole-brain task effect).

The study uses fMRI during a social-cognition task (sarcasm detection/mentalizing), satisfying I3. Participants are healthy adults (n=20, ages 19–29), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts for healthy participants: Analysis 17092490_analysis_1 (S1 whole-brain, FWE-corrected voxel-level results, reported peaks) and Analysis 17092490_analysis_2 (sarcasm detection S; NS > UC, whole-brain, FWE-corrected voxel-level results, reported peaks), satisfying I5. Although an ROI/VOI analysis is also reported (Analysis 0), whole-brain results are present, so E2 is not met. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study examines passive observation of social interactions (relational vs alone segments) using video clips—clearly a social-related task. Participants are healthy adults (mean age 27.2), satisfying the age criterion. The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrast (relational > alone) with whole-brain inference corrected for multiple comparisons and reports peak coordinates. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply. Full text is available in the provided record.

The study used task-based fMRI probing social cognition (listening to film excerpts and inferring characters’ mental states), includes a healthy adult group (n=28; mean age 37.6) reported separately, and reports a whole-brain, group-level within-group contrast for the healthy controls (French story > Hindi story; one-sample t-test; inference over whole brain; FWE-corrected results and peak table). Whole-brain results for the healthy group are clearly presented, satisfying the review’s requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

Exclusion E4 met: the NeuroStore record shows only omnibus between-group/interactions (Group × Scan × Stimulus Group) contrasts and peak tables; no unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps are reported. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: analyses labelled “Social Interaction Analysis” using IAPS social/positive images). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (although healthy adults are included, the record does not report healthy-group results separately from patient vs control contrasts), I5 (no group-level, whole‑brain task-evoked map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group). Therefore the paper must be excluded because it reports only between-group/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect (E4).

This fMRI study examines social processing (dynamic facial expressions with social interaction cues) and includes a healthy adult control group, but the NeuroStore record only reports whole-brain between-group contrasts and interaction effects or effects across all participants. There is no clearly identified, unmasked whole-brain task activation map reported specifically for the healthy/control group (non-SPD) in the extract. Therefore it fails the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task effect. Exclusion is based on E4 (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported without an accompanying unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task map). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult participants included). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly identified healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map). I6 not satisfied because qualifying whole-brain results for the healthy group are not clearly described as coming from the healthy/control group in the record.

This fMRI hyperscanning study used an interactive social task (Prisoner’s Dilemma) and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise GLM results (contrasts with reported peak coordinates and whole-brain inference using permutation TFCE). Sample is healthy adults (n=44, mean age 22.37, range within 18–65). Whole-brain analyses and coordinate tables are provided (Tables tb1–tb3), satisfying acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, and it is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, ages within 18–65, and empirical fMRI data present). The sample is healthy adults (n=16, mean age 26.1, within 18–65) (I4). Multiple group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts/F-tests are reported with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference (voxelwise and clusterwise FWE correction) and coordinates/peaks are provided (I5, I6). NeuroStore extract lists several whole-brain contrasts (e.g., omnibus F-tests and pairwise within-group contrasts) with reported peaks and MNI coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age, or non-empirical study). Minor note: the record does not explicitly state the word “healthy,” but participants are described as volunteers with typical adult ages and no clinical groups reported, so inclusion is appropriate.

The study uses task-based fMRI of social cognition (ostension/interaction vs observation) in healthy adult participants (mean age 25, n=11–22 reported), satisfying I3 and I4. NeuroStore indicates model fit over the whole brain and reports voxelwise between-condition contrasts with reported peaks (analyses 23267322_analysis_0 and _6: whole-brain voxel-level results without ROI restriction), which satisfy I5 and I6 (coordinates/peaks reported). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion requirements for the review.

The study reports fMRI during a social interaction task (reciprocal imitation), meeting social-related task requirement. Results are reported in tables/coordinates, acceptable per I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only without whole-brain activations, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study used task-based fMRI (EmpaToM; BOLD responses) probing social affect and Theory of Mind (I3). The analyses are second-level, voxelwise, whole-brain group regressions with reported peak coordinates (model fit over: whole brain; peaks in Table t1), satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting in tables/figures (I5,I6). Analyses are within-group associations (not restricted to ROIs or connectivity-only results). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears sufficiently represented in this document.

The NeuroStore record indicates this is an fMRI hyperscanning study of social interaction (mutual gaze and joint attention), satisfying I3. The record lists group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (e.g., GLM contrast for eye-blink onset MG2 and a visual category localizer) with reported peak coordinates and whole-brain inference, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only without whole-brain task maps, between-group-only, age out of range, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study uses task fMRI of a social interaction (handshake) and includes a healthy adult control group, but the paper does not report a group-level, whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The only whole-brain result is an omnibus between-group test; the healthy-group-specific results are reported only as region-of-interest post-hoc contrasts. Therefore the study violates exclusion criterion E4 (between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social fMRI task) and I4 (healthy adult group reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain healthy/control group task map) and I6 (no evidence that a qualifying whole-brain healthy-group result is reported in any format). Consequently the study should be excluded.

This study reports an fMRI experiment using a social interaction task (virtual ball-toss) and clearly involves social cognition (I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (mean age 21.24, n=31), meeting the age/sample requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (random-effects paired t tests; whole-brain model fit; cluster-level FWE thresholding, reported peaks/tables), providing unmasked healthy-group whole-brain results (I5,I6). Analyses also include tables of reported peaks (Table t1). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity-only (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E4), and participants are within 18–65 (E5). Full text is available in the extracted record, so fulltext_incomplete=false. Based on these points, the study satisfies all inclusion criteria and should be included.

The study uses task-based functional MRI during a clearly social task (Ultimatum Game) and reports whole-brain, group-level multivariate classification results with peak coordinates/tables. NeuroStore indicates whole-brain model fitting and reported peaks (tables), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement; coordinate reporting is acceptable per I6. Although the sample is small (n=7) and there is an extraction inconsistency in the sex counts (n reported as 7 but ‘‘0 female, 10 male’’), the document provides sufficient information that a healthy adult group was analyzed and whole-brain results are reported. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical study) are met.

The study uses task fMRI of social-related processing (self/other referential judgments) meeting I3. It reports a healthy control group (TD; mean age 27.25, range includes adults) reported separately from the ASD group, satisfying I4. The paper provides whole-brain, group-level within-group contrasts for the healthy (TD) group (TD Self>Letter and TD Other>Letter) with reported peaks, meeting I5. Whole-brain results are presented as coordinate tables/peaks, which is acceptable per I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E2), not limited to connectivity/resting-state (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E4), and the study includes adult participants (not exclusively outside 18–65; E5 not applicable). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

The study used fMRI during a naturalistic social cognition task (mental state judgments of social scenes and Cyberball Social Exclusion), reported BOLD responses, and tested healthy adults (n=38, age 18–30). Multiple main-effect contrasts (e.g., Social > Non-social scenes; Table 1) list reported peaks consistent with group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (coordinates reported), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps; coordinate tables are acceptable. Although one analysis was an ROI correlation (OFC), the presence of whole-brain main-effect peaks meets inclusion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears available in the record.

This fMRI study includes healthy adult participants (ages ~20.6–20.7) who performed a task involving sign language processing and grammaticality judgment—falling under social communication relevant to social-related processing (I3). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were performed (one-sample t-tests) with reported whole-brain peaks/tables for each healthy group (DVD-exposure n=21; live-exposure n=18), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5) and the sample criterion (I4). Coordinate results are reported (tables of peaks), consistent with I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity/resting-state only (E3), and include within-group whole-brain effects rather than only between-group contrasts (not E4). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This study uses fMRI of a social task (Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy adult participants and reports whole-brain peaks; however the reported whole-brain contrasts extracted are between-group interaction effects (treatment by OXTR methylation) rather than a group-level task-evoked main effect or within-group contrast for the healthy/control group. According to the review criteria, studies that report only between-group contrasts or interactions without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect must be excluded (E4). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported), I6 (whole-brain results reported in tables). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no clear group-level, whole-brain task-evoked map/main effect from the healthy group). Therefore the paper is excluded under E4.

The study reports fMRI BOLD responses during a clearly social cognition task (observing cooperative and affective social interactions), satisfying I3. The sample is 36 healthy participants (reported as healthy adults), satisfying I4 (healthy adult group reported separately). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) within-group contrasts and parametric modulations with model fit and inference over the whole brain and tables of reported peaks, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply: whole-brain results are present (so not E2/E3), results are within-group healthy participants (not only between-group; not E4), participants are described as healthy adults (no E5), and this is original empirical fMRI data (not E6).

This study reports task-evoked BOLD fMRI during processing of emotional prosody—a social-communication task—using healthy adult participants (n=13, ages 18–60). NeuroStore extraction indicates group-level, whole-brain (model fit over: whole brain) voxelwise contrasts (random effects GLM) with reported peak coordinates for multiple within-group contrasts. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), and whole-brain group-level results reported (I5). Whole-brain results in coordinate tables are acceptable (I6). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, age out of range, or non-empirical) are met.

The study used task-based BOLD fMRI during a social-related biological motion perception task contrasting social interaction (SI) vs non-social interaction (NSI), satisfying I3. The sample is 14 healthy adults (mean age 29.4, within 18–65), satisfying I4. The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise within-group contrast (SI>NSI) with inference over the whole brain (FDR-corrected p<0.05) and lists 24 peak coordinates in MNI space, satisfying I5 and I6. The reported model is a one-sample t-test/GLM on the healthy group. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants within age range, and empirical fMRI data are reported). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study used task-based fMRI to investigate action anticipation/prediction of others’ actions (sport-specific free-throw prediction), which falls under perception and understanding of others (social-related processing). Participants are healthy adults in the 18–65 range (experts: n=16, ages 19–30; novices: n=16, ages 19–37). The NeuroStore extraction reports voxelwise whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference and provides group-level within-group contrasts for both experts and novices (Analyses 1 and 2) with reported peaks/tables, meeting the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps from healthy groups. Results are reported in tables of peaks. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-only, between-group-only without healthy-group maps, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This fMRI study directly investigates social cognition (understanding others' mental states) using a well-established false-belief task, reporting event-related BOLD activations. The reported analysis is a within-group whole-brain contrast (ROMS > CTRL) with voxelwise model fitting and whole-brain inference (FDR-corrected p<0.05; peaks reported in a table). The sample is healthy adults (n=34; ages 20–28). Therefore it meets the review's requirements for a social-task fMRI study in healthy adults with whole-brain group-level task activation results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-adult sample, or non-empirical) are met.

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it reports task-based fMRI during social interaction perception (I3), includes a healthy adult sample (n=34, ages 20–35) reported separately (I4), and presents whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts with peak coordinates and whole-brain inference (I5). Reporting of coordinates/tables satisfies acceptable reporting (I6). No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are whole-brain task-evoked contrasts rather than ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-adult-only, or non-empirical. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social processing (gaze perception/joint attention and mental-inference tasks), satisfying social-related task requirement. The sample consists of healthy adults (ages 19–28) with group results reported. Multiple group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses are reported (model fit over whole brain; within-group contrasts and cross-subject regressions with voxel- and cluster-level thresholds; reported peak coordinates/tables), fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement and acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, ages within 18–65, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

The study reports a task involving social perception (viewing dyadic biological-motion displays while performing an incidental task), acquired with fMRI (BOLD). The sample is healthy adults (n=10, ages 22–32). The analyses are whole-brain second-level random-effects voxelwise contrasts ((atypical-upright + atypical-inverted) - (typical-upright + typical-inverted)) with whole-brain inference and tables of reported peak coordinates (Talairach), satisfying whole-brain reporting. Thresholding and reported peak tables confirm task-evoked whole-brain results for the healthy group. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within 18–65, empirical fMRI data). Therefore the paper meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the review.

The study used fMRI during a social-related empathy-for-pain task with healthy adult participants (n=23, ages 19–34), satisfying I3 and I4. However, the NeuroStore record shows the reported analysis was a region-of-interest analysis (model fit over: region of interest) and does not provide any group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked maps for the healthy group. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only reporting). Based on the provided document, no whole-brain healthy-group task activation map is available, so the study is excluded.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social processing (gaze perception/joint attention). The sample is healthy adults (n=12, ages 18–40), satisfying the age and healthy-sample criterion. NeuroStore extraction shows whole-brain model fits and group-level, voxelwise within-subject contrasts (multiple reported contrasts with voxelwise thresholds and tables of peaks), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps (reported peaks/tables meet acceptable reporting modes). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) fMRI was used during a social interaction task (Prisoner’s Dilemma; in-group/out-group interactions). (I4) Samples are healthy adults (Experiment 1: n=20, mean age 20.8; Experiment 2: n=30, mean age 21.2). (I5) The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps (e.g., PD > Gamble, one-sample t-tests, model fit over whole brain, reported coordinate peaks/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, includes within-group whole-brain contrasts, ages within 18–65, empirical fMRI data). Therefore include for the meta-analysis of social processing in healthy adults.

The study meets all required inclusion criteria: it uses fMRI during a social-related task (face encoding/social cognition) (I3); reports results for a healthy adult control group (n=11, age mean 18.7) separately from the clinical FXS group (I4); reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise within-group activation maps for the healthy/control group (Analysis 18778781_analysis_1; model fit and inference over whole brain) satisfying whole-brain evidence (I5); and such whole-brain results are clearly described (I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered: results are not limited to ROIs, not only connectivity/resting-state, and a healthy adult group whole-brain task effect is reported. Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

The study uses fMRI during a social evaluative task (faces trustworthiness/age), and reports a separate healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, all reported analyses were fit and/or inferred within pre-specified regions of interest (Model fit over: region of interest; inference restricted to ROI for within-group maps). No whole-brain (voxelwise, unmasked) group-level healthy-control task activation map is reported. Therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses, no whole-brain results).

This study examined social processing (viewing political candidates' faces) in healthy adults and reports whole-brain voxelwise results (peak tables). However, all reported group-level maps in the NeuroStore record are between-group contrasts/interactions (party × candidate interaction) or cross-subject regressions (associations with rating covariates). There is no clear unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect or simple within-group main effect (e.g., faces > baseline or within-group candidate contrasts) reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interactions without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I6 (coordinates/tables reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no clear whole-brain healthy-group task map).

The paper uses fMRI during a social-communication task (gesture/body orientation) and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the NeuroStore extract shows only whole-brain conjunctions across groups and between-group interaction contrasts (conjunctions like (HS ∩ MDD) and interactions patient>control or control>patient). There is no unmasked, whole-brain, within-group healthy-control task activation map (e.g., HS: IC>NG or Fro>Lat reported for healthy participants alone) identified in the document or tables/figures. Therefore the study reports only between-group/intersection results without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect, meeting exclusion criterion E4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clearly identified whole-brain healthy-group task map) and I6 (no qualifying healthy-group whole-brain results reported in tables/figures). Decision: EXCLUDED.

Study reports task-based fMRI of attachment (a social-related construct) in healthy adults (N=25, ages 19–26). Whole-brain, second-level voxelwise analyses were performed and contrasts within the healthy group (attachment vs control; subanalyses monadic/dyadic and interaction) are reported with peak coordinates and cluster-level correction. This satisfies all inclusion criteria and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=13, ages 19–36) using a social cognition task (Theory of Mind and empathy comic-strip task). NeuroStore extraction shows multiple group-level, within-group contrasts and a conjunction, with the model fit and inference reported over the whole brain and peak coordinates listed in tables (Talairach space). These meet the meta-analysis objective and the requirement for whole-brain, task-evoked healthy-group results. The article is empirical, not ROI- or connectivity-only, and the healthy-group results are reported separately. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. It used task-based fMRI of social cognition (ToM and empathy) (I3). The sample is a healthy participant group of college students with ages spanning 17–21 (majority adults), providing a healthy adult group relevant to the review (I4). The paper reports multiple group-level, whole-brain, within-group task-evoked contrasts (one-sample t-tests for ToM > Physical and Empathy > Physical) with whole-brain model fitting and thresholded results/peak coordinates in tables (I5). Coordinates/peaks are reported in tables, which is acceptable per I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, and not non-empirical. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study meets inclusion criteria: (I3) participants viewed movies depicting emotional/social interactions—task involves perception/understanding of others; (I4) sample includes healthy adults (n=16, ages 25–49); (I5) reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (intersubject correlations computed and tested over the whole brain, voxelwise FDR thresholding); (I6) whole-brain results are clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed-only, reports healthy-group whole-brain effects).

The study reports fMRI during a social-related task (encoding social interactions; egocentric vs allocentric communication contexts), includes a healthy adult sample (n=18, mean age 24.1, ages 20–30), and presents multiple group-level, whole-brain within-group task contrasts (e.g., CC> M, IC> M, CC>IC, IC>CC) with inference over the whole brain. Results are reported as voxelwise contrasts (MNI space) with thresholding details and peak coordinates. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for the review (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria. The NeuroStore extract is treated as the fulltext for screening per instructions.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a virtual social cognition task (social attribution of avatars), includes a healthy adult group (n=14, mean age 27.5), and provides whole-brain, voxelwise within-group healthy-control activation maps with reported peak coordinates (Table tbl2) in Talairach space. Thus it meets I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately), I5 (whole-brain group-level healthy-task map), and I6 (coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting/connectivity-only, healthy-group whole-brain effects are present, ages within 18–65, empirical fMRI data).

Exclusion met: E2 (study reports inference restricted to regions-of-interest with FWE small-volume correction and no unmasked whole-brain task activation map is presented). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task is a social-cognition/ToM task — Reading the Mind in the Eyes) and I4 (healthy adult sample, n=18, mean age 26.4). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported — inference was restricted to ROIs/SVC). Although the model was fit over the whole brain, all reported inference used ROI small-volume correction, and reported peaks appear limited to those ROIs; thus the paper provides ROI-only inference rather than unmasked whole-brain results required by I5/I6. fulltext_incomplete=false

The study reports an fMRI face-perception task in healthy adults and provides group-level whole-brain task activation results. The faces>houses within-group contrast was estimated across the whole brain at second level (n=22 healthy adults) with reported peak coordinates (Table) and FWE thresholding. Face perception maps onto social-related processing (Perception and Understanding of Others). All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The NeuroStore record shows the study used task-based fMRI of social cognition (dynamic facial expressions/social interaction) in healthy adult participants (n=17, mean age 25.9). It reports a group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrast (SOC > ARB) from a second-level ANOVA/FIR model with results reported (peaks in Table 1; MNI coordinates) and voxelwise thresholding (p<0.001, cluster extent). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked map), and I6 (whole-brain results reported as peaks/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears available in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults (n=16, mean age 20) using a social working memory task involving friends’ names and trait judgments, which is clearly a social-related paradigm. NeuroStore indicates group-level, whole-brain (model fit and inference over whole brain, MNI coordinates) voxelwise analyses (parametric load regressors and cross-subject regression with perspective-taking scores) reported as peaks, meeting the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. All inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3: social fMRI task; I4: healthy adult sample 18–65; I5: group-level whole-brain voxelwise results; I6: whole-brain results reported as coordinates). No exclusion criteria apply. Although sample size is modest, that does not conflict with eligibility. Full text is available in the provided record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study uses fMRI during tasks probing social cognition (personal prayer vs others) and authors specifically interpret recruitment of social-cognition areas, satisfying I3. Sample is healthy adults (n=20, ages 21–32), satisfying I4. Multiple group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and main effects are reported with inference over the whole brain and tables of peak coordinates, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity/resting-state only (E3), include within-group whole-brain effects (not only between-group; E4), participants are within 18–65 (E5), and this is empirical fMRI data (not E6). Therefore include. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I6. Exclusion criteria met: none.

The study reports task-based fMRI (BOLD) during a social interaction task (matching-pennies with human, android, robots, computer) and analyzes impressions of others—meeting the social-processing requirement. Participants are healthy adults (n=16; ages 18–25), satisfying the sample criterion. NeuroStore extraction indicates whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference (random-effects group GLM, one-sample t-tests) with reported peak coordinates/tables, satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. Thresholding and group-level results are clearly described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, and participants are within 18–65). Full text appears sufficiently available in the record. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates none; it should be INCLUDED.

This study is excluded because it reports only region-of-interest (ROI)-restricted analyses and does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise healthy-group task activation map. Evidence: NeuroStore fields show 'Model fit over: region of interest' and 'Inference restricted to: region of interest' for the reported contrasts, region-level thresholding, and the abstract states analyses focused on STS/STG. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task - watching social/traffic campaign videos) and I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately: n=25/44, ages within 18–65). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear whole-brain group-level task-evoked map for the healthy/control group). Exclusion criteria met: E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Therefore the study does not satisfy the whole-brain evidence requirement and is excluded.

Excluded for E4. The study uses task fMRI of social interaction (I3 met). However, the NeuroStore record does not report any group-level, unmasked whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Reported whole-brain maps are for all subjects combined or for interaction contrasts, and the healthy-group results are presented only as ROI-restricted or as between-group contrasts (Healthy Controls > ASD). Therefore the paper fails to meet I5 (healthy-group whole-brain evidence) and does not provide a clear healthy adult group whole-brain map (I4 not satisfied as reported). Exclusion criteria applied: E4 (between-group/interaction results without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5.

This study meets the review objective and inclusion criteria: (I3) It uses task-based fMRI during a social interaction paradigm (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma). (I5) It reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results (GLM random-effects analyses with whole-brain inference and FWE-corrected cluster-level results; reported peaks/tables). (I4) The sample consists of 153 healthy male participants (no indication of clinical or special groups); while exact ages are not reported in the NeuroStore record, participants are described as adult participants in the context of the study and no evidence indicates they fall outside 18–65. No exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded per E2: NeuroStore indicates the study used fMRI during a social cognition task (I3) on a healthy adult sample (I4), but inference was restricted to a region-of-interest and only ROI-restricted significant peaks are reported. The record does not provide an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map or whole-brain results for the healthy group, so inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain group-level evidence) is not met (and I6 is not satisfied). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only reporting).

The study reports task-based fMRI measuring perception of social interactions (threatening vs non-threatening interpersonal encounters), satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adults (n=16; ages 22–34), satisfying I4. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts are reported (model fit and inference over whole brain; whole-brain cluster-corrected thresholding; peak coordinates in Table 1), meeting I5 and I6. Results are not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, or non-empirical; no exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

The study meets the review inclusion criteria: it used fMRI during a clearly social-related task (social working memory with trait-ranking of participants’ close friends and perspective-taking demands), included a healthy adult sample (n=25, mean age 21.56 within 18–65), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation results (model fit and inference over the whole brain, cluster-corrected thresholding, and reported peaks). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and is empirical). The NeuroStore record appears to provide complete group-level whole-brain contrast information for the healthy sample.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=22, mean age 24.36). Tasks are social-cognitive (mind perception and gaze-cuing). Analyses are within-group, parametric whole-brain voxelwise models (model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain) with reported peak coordinates/tables, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) are met and no exclusions are triggered.

This study meets all inclusion criteria. It uses fMRI during a clearly social task (Prisoner’s Dilemma) assessing social behaviour and social cognition (I3). It includes a healthy adult group (n=15; mean age 34.07, SD 6.05) reported separately (I4). Crucially, the paper reports a whole-brain, group-level, within-group healthy-controls task contrast (Analysis 31598216_analysis_3: CONTROLS; whole-brain model fit; reported peaks), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked activation maps (I5). Results are reported as coordinate peaks/tables (acceptable per I6). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-only; healthy-group whole-brain effects are provided; participants are within 18–65; and the paper is empirical).

The study used fMRI during a social cognition task (valence classification of agentic vs communal trait words), satisfying I3. Participants were healthy adults (mean age 21.05, range 18–25), satisfying I4. The manuscript reports group-level task contrasts (comparisons to implicit baseline and fixation) with tables of peak coordinates, and at least one analysis indicates model fitting over the whole brain; these reported whole-brain contrasts (tables of peaks) meet I5 and are acceptable per I6 (coordinate tables). Although one analysis used ROI-restricted inference, other contrasts are presented as whole-brain results in tables, so the paper is not limited to ROI-only inference. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports task-based fMRI using social stimuli (implicit emotional face processing with gaze/head orientation), satisfying I3. The sample comprises healthy adult males (mean age ~30), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts for the healthy groups (e.g., within-group contrast in NFS only, whole-brain model fit, reported peaks/tables), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results include whole-brain healthy-group activation maps (not ROI-only or connectivity-only), participants are within 18–65, and the paper is empirical. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusions apply.

Exclusion E4 applies: the paper reports only between-group contrasts/interactions for task activity (group × condition interaction and HC vs SZ contrasts) and does not present an unmasked, whole-brain task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are met (fMRI during a social-cognitive task; healthy adult participants included). Inclusion criterion I5 is not met (no whole-brain, group-level healthy-control task effect reported). Full text appears complete in this record. Therefore the study must be excluded under E4.

Exclusion E4 applies: the NeuroStore record reports only between-group contrasts/interactions (gain-group main effects and interactions) and PPI connectivity, but does not report an unmasked whole-brain task activation map for the healthy group (e.g., a main effect of unfair>fair across all participants). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a clearly social task — Ultimatum Game with online negotiations), I4 (healthy adult sample reported, n=54), and I6 (whole-brain results are reported as coordinate tables). Inclusion criterion I5 is not met because there is no clearly described whole-group, voxelwise task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group separate from subgroup (LG/HG) contrasts. Therefore the study must be excluded under E4.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social interaction (friendship/affiliation/empathy) meeting I3. Sample consists of healthy adults (n=28, ages 19–27), meeting I4. Analyses are voxelwise, second-level random-effects GLM with model fit over the whole brain and cluster-level FWE thresholding; results are reported as peak coordinates/tables, satisfying I5 and acceptable under I6. No exclusion criteria are met: this is not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity/resting-state-only (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E4), ages are within 18–65 (E5), and the paper is empirical (E6). Thus all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusions apply.

The study reports fMRI during a social-related task (face emotion discrimination) in a healthy adult sample (n=30, mean age ~31.5), and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., EE>baseline and EE>EI; one-sample t-tests; analyses 0 and 1) with reported peak coordinates. Whole-brain results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group and are reported at voxelwise thresholding and in tables of peaks. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, and not only between-group contrasts).

This study meets I3 (uses fMRI during a social-related task: Emotional Face Matching with angry/fearful faces) and I4 (healthy adult sample, n=15, mean age 26.7). However, NeuroStore indicates all reported group analyses were conducted and inferred only within an amygdala region-of-interest (model fit over ROI; inference restricted to ROI; thresholding corrected within amygdala). No group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group is reported. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met, and exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results) applies. fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: task involves narrative reading eliciting suspense which the authors link to social-cognitive processes (perception/understanding of others), sample consists of healthy adults (n=23, ages 19–32), and the paper reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps (reading > rating and a parametric modulation by suspense) with whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages are within 18–65, and the paper reports original fMRI data. Therefore include.

The study examines social/attachment processing (mothers viewing own child/dog), so I3 is met. The sample is healthy adults (n=14, ages 28–44), so I4 is met. However, all reported analyses in the NeuroStore record state 'Model fit over: region of interest' and 'Inference restricted to: region of interest' with small-volume FWE correction, and no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked maps are reported. Therefore the paper does not provide the required whole-brain healthy-group task activation (I5 not met). This triggers exclusion E2 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete in the record. Excluded for E2.

The study uses fMRI during a social decision-making task (I3) and includes a healthy young adult group (ages 21–22) (I4). Results are reported in coordinate tables/peaks (I6). However, no whole-brain, group-level task activation map is reported specifically for the healthy adult group alone; the paper reports whole-brain within-group contrasts for all participants combined and reports subgroup effects only as between-group interactions (adolescents > young adults; young adults > adolescents). Therefore it lacks an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-adult task effect required by I5, meeting exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts for the adult subgroup without an accompanying adult-group whole-brain map).

This study uses task-based fMRI of a clearly social-related paradigm (the Multifaceted Empathy Test assessing cognitive and emotional empathy), meeting I3. It includes a separate healthy adult control group (n=29; mean age 27.9, within 18–65) reported separately from the BPD group, meeting I4. Importantly, the record reports group-level, whole-brain, within-group task contrasts for control subjects (e.g., Analysis 21586330_analysis_8: control subjects, cognitive empathy > physical appearance inference; Model fit over: whole brain; reported peaks), and likewise for emotional empathy contrasts (Analyses 11 and 12), satisfying I5 (and acceptable reporting per I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the paper meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This fMRI study examines observational understanding of toolmaking, explicitly addressing mentalizing and motor resonance (social-cognition constructs: perception/understanding of others). Participants are healthy adults (n=26). NeuroStore reports whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference (FDR-corrected maps, cluster extent), and the abstract and results describe effects “across subject groups” (Acheulean > Oldowan) linking activations to social-cognitive processes; multiple whole-brain group-level contrasts and coordinate tables (reported peaks) are provided. Thus the paper reports at least one group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map clearly coming from the healthy participant sample. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not patient-only, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria are met.

Exclusion E4 applies: the paper does not report a whole-brain group-level task activation map specifically for the healthy/control group (full-term mothers). While the study reports a whole-brain map for 'all mothers' (Analysis 0) and reports between-group ROI contrasts (PT>FT, FT>PT) restricted to insula/parahippocampal ROI, it lacks an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group (FT) task effect. Inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are met (social/attachment face-processing task; healthy adult participants—full-term mothers reported as without disorders). Inclusion criterion I5 is NOT met (no whole-brain healthy-group map reported). Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study uses fMRI during a social-emotional, face-to-face simulated interaction task (actresses describing happy/sad experiences), meeting I3. Participants are healthy adults (n=20, mean age 33), meeting I4. Analyses were fit over the whole brain and report group-level voxelwise task contrasts with peak coordinates (Talairach) and cluster-thresholded results (bootstrap p<0.05, cluster extent), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity/resting-only (E3), and not only between-group contrasts (E4). Thus all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 are met and no exclusions are triggered.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social judgment task (evaluation of social dominance in faces), meeting the social-related task requirement (I3). The sample comprises 23 healthy adults aged 21–43, satisfying the healthy adult sample criterion (I4). The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrast (Social Judgment > Perceptual Judgment) with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference using a one-sample t-test and cluster FWE thresholding; results/peaks are listed in Table 1, meeting whole-brain evidence criteria (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears sufficiently represented in the supplied document.

This study used task-based fMRI with established social-cognition tasks (Reading the Mind in the Eyes; False Belief), meeting social-related task requirement. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=14, mean age 28.4) reported separately. NeuroStore extraction shows model fit over the whole brain for within-group regression analyses and reports peak coordinates for the control group (Tables), satisfying the requirement for at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked result. Results for the healthy group are clearly identified (Controls BET vs TABS; Controls EToM vs TABS). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and not limited to between-group contrasts. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be included.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) It used task-based fMRI of social communication (gaze- and pointing-finger cues). (I4) Reports a healthy adult sample (n=17, ages 20–34). (I5) Reports at least one group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrast (finger pointing > gaze following) with model fit and inference over the whole brain. (I6) Whole-brain results/peaks are reported (Talairach coordinates, cluster‐level correction). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity/resting-state only (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E4), participants are within 18–65 (E5), and it is empirical fMRI data (not a review) (E6). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

The study uses an empathy-for-pain fMRI task (I3 satisfied) and includes healthy adult participants, but the NeuroStore record reports only between-group (patient vs control / interaction) whole-brain contrasts. No unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map or within-group healthy control maps are reported in the document. This violates inclusion criteria I4 (results for healthy group reported separately) and I5 (healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Therefore exclusion criterion E4 applies (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain effect).

The study used task-based fMRI to examine perception/understanding of others (threatening vs teasing interactions), meeting the social-processing requirement. Participants are healthy adults (n=14, mean age 23.6), with group results reported for this healthy sample. Multiple group-level, whole-brain within-group contrasts are reported (e.g., Threat>tease, Emotion>color) with model fit and inference performed over the whole brain and peaks listed in tables, satisfying whole-brain reporting and acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no resting-state/seed-only, no only between-group contrasts, and participants are within 18–65). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports task-based fMRI of a social-related paradigm (anticipation of touching an animate/human hand vs inanimate mannequin), meeting the review focus on social processing. The sample comprises healthy adults (n=21; ages 21–33), satisfying the age and healthy-group requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation analyses (paired-sample t-tests and one-sample t-tests with covariates) with peaks listed in a table, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement; results are clearly described and reported in tables. No exclusion criteria are met: the report is not ROI-only, includes task-evoked whole-brain maps (not only resting-state or connectivity), and presents within-group healthy subject effects. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.

The study used task-based fMRI during a social cognition task (trustworthiness ratings/face perception; Implicit Association Task) in healthy adult participants (n=30; ages 18–29), satisfying I3 and I4. The NeuroStore record indicates model fitting over the whole brain and whole-brain inference for multiple group-level, second-level covariate analyses with reported peak coordinates in tables, meeting the requirement for at least one group-level whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (I5) and acceptable reporting formats (I6). No exclusion criteria apply: results are not limited to ROIs only (E2), are not only connectivity without whole-brain activation maps (E3), are not only between-group contrasts (E4), and participants are within the 18–65 range (E5).

The study used task-based fMRI of charitable donation decisions, a form of social decision-making engaging social-cognition constructs (meets I3). The sample is healthy adults (n=22; ages 19–38), within 18–65 (meets I4). Multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results are reported (e.g., parametric modulation of subjective value, free>forced contrast, willingness-to-give regression) with whole-brain cluster correction (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and this is empirical fMRI data. Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) task is social-cognitive impression formation (people vs objects) using fMRI; (I4) sample are healthy adults (n=14; ages 18.3–23.7); (I5) reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task effects (model fit over whole brain; voxel-level thresholding; coordinate tables/peaks reported); (I6) whole-brain results are reported as peak coordinates/tables. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity/resting-state only (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E4), participants are within 18–65 (E5), and this is empirical fMRI data (not a review; E6). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Study used task-based fMRI probing social-affective mimicry (imitation-inhibition with facial expressions), with healthy adult participants (n=41; mean age 22.6). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses were conducted (random-effects second-level GLM/ANOVA), inference reported over the whole brain with peak coordinates/tables for contrasts (Incongruent>Congruent and emotion/group-specific masked contrasts). Results are reported as whole-brain activation maps (tables of peaks) for the healthy sample. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants in age range, empirical fMRI data).

The study reports task-based fMRI during social cognition (empathy-evoking film clips with contextual cues and music), meeting the review topic. Participants are healthy adults (n=26, mean age 30.3, within 18–65). The NeuroStore record shows group-level whole-brain task results (Analysis 26604273_analysis_1 and analysis_2 report inference over the whole brain with FWE-corrected thresholds), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked maps. Although the paper also reports ROI and effective-connectivity (DCM) analyses, these are not exclusive and do not preclude inclusion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study used fMRI during a social perception task (meets I3) and includes a healthy adult control group with results reported separately (meets I4). However, all reported analyses were region-of-interest (ROI) based with inference restricted to predefined ROIs using small-volume correction (no unmasked, whole-brain/voxelwise healthy-group activation maps reported). Therefore it fails to meet I5 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results). Full text appears complete for screening.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=28, ages 18–40) performing social tasks (Dictator Game and a self-referential localizer), addressing social processing. It includes at least one group-level, whole-brain, within-group contrast (Self > Syllables) analyzed with a second-level random-effects model and reported peaks, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Reporting of peaks meets acceptable formats for whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adults within 18–65, and is empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria relevant to the review are satisfied and the study should be INCLUDED.

This study uses fMRI during a social cognitive task (facial emotion recognition with introspective accuracy judgments), includes a healthy adult group (n=32; mean age ~35) with results reported separately, and reports at least one group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) within-group contrast for the healthy participants (IA > control) with cluster-level correction and reported peak coordinates. The task and measures clearly index social processing, and whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps are provided in tables/coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, includes unmasked healthy-group whole-brain effect, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical fMRI data).

The study reports fMRI of a social cognition (False Belief/Theory-of-Mind) task involving cooperation vs competition (meets I3). Participants are healthy adults (n=18, ages 21–38), meeting the 18–65 criterion (I4). The paper reports multiple group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts with inference over the whole brain (FWE cluster correction), and reports peak coordinates in MNI space (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, and empirical fMRI data present).

The study uses task-based BOLD fMRI during social cognition tasks (face-based approachability and intelligence judgements) (I3). It reports healthy adult groups (22 females, 25 males; ages ~31–33) separately from the ASD group (I4). Multiple group-level, within-group whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts for healthy participants are reported (e.g., males and females within-group activations; inference over whole brain; reported peak coordinate tables), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5). Results are reported as thresholded whole-brain contrasts with peak tables, acceptable per I6. The paper also includes clinical groups but reports healthy-group whole-brain results separately. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without healthy whole-brain effect, age out of range, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

Exclusion E4 met: the study includes healthy control participants and reports between-group contrasts, but does not report any group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy/control group. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social evaluative task) and I4 (healthy adult participants reported separately). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task map reported). Full text appears complete for screening.

The study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria: (I3) uses fMRI during a social-related Theory of Mind task; (I4) includes a healthy adult group reported separately (n=19, mean age 33.5); (I5) reports a whole-brain, group-level within-group contrast for controls (ToM > Random) with whole-brain inference and thresholding (FDR-corrected, peaks reported); (I6) whole-brain results are clearly described. No exclusion criteria apply: the paper includes whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps (so E2, E3, E4 do not apply), participants are within the 18–65 range (E5 not met), and it is an empirical fMRI study (E6 not met).

This study uses an interactive competitive fMRI task (socially interactive) in a healthy adult sample (n=69, mean age ~26), so it meets I3 (social-related task) and I4 (healthy adult sample). However, the NeuroStore record indicates reported analyses were conducted within a region-of-interest (Reward-mask) with inference restricted to that ROI; no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) healthy-group task activation map is reported. Therefore it does not meet I5 (whole-brain evidence). This matches exclusion criterion E2 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Based on these facts the paper must be excluded.

This fMRI study tests neural responses to angry vs. neutral facial expressions within an interactive social task (Taylor Aggression Paradigm), addressing social perception/response to others (meets I3). The sample comprises healthy adults (n=32 analyzed, mean age 23.3), meeting the age and healthy-sample requirement (I4). Models were fit over the whole brain and inference was performed whole-brain with reported group-level contrasts (Angry>Neutral) and reported peak coordinates/tables, providing unmasked, whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy group (I5, I6). The NeuroStore extract shows one-sample GLM contrasts and parametric analyses with whole-brain FWE thresholding and tables of peaks. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group–only, participants within age range, empirical fMRI data present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of social cognition (EmpaToM manipulating empathy and Theory of Mind), reporting group-level, whole-brain within-group contrasts. Multiple analyses (including N=178) report whole-brain, FWE-corrected results with peak coordinates/tables. Samples are healthy adults (n=25 and n=178; mean ages 32.6 and 40.9, within 18–65). Results are clearly from the healthy/control group and are reported as tables of peaks. Thus the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study examines social communication (perception of being addressed via body orientation and co-speech gesture), meeting the review’s topical requirement. Participants are healthy adults (n=37; ages 20–39), satisfying the sample inclusion. The NeuroStore record indicates whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference for group-level task contrasts (multiple within-group contrasts reported with tables of peaks and cluster-level correction), fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked results from the healthy group. Results are reported as coordinate tables and described in the abstract. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-empirical, or out-of-range ages) are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied.

This study uses fMRI of a clearly social task (social influence/adaptation to group opinions) and reports results from healthy adult participants (n=24), but it does not provide an unmasked whole-brain group-level task activation map. All extracted analyses indicate the model was fit over the whole brain but inference was restricted to regions of interest with FWE small-volume correction (i.e., ROI-restricted inference). Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only reporting). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. No other exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports an fMRI experiment of affective touch (a social/affiliative processing task) in healthy adult participants (n=40, mean age 21.19). Multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked contrasts are reported (e.g., Positive>Neutral, OT>PLC, OTnegative>PLCnegative) with whole-brain inference (FDR p<0.05, cluster extent) and tables of peak coordinates (Table tbl0001). The record also contains ROI connectivity results, but whole-brain healthy-group activation maps are clearly reported. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria (E2–E6).

The study uses fMRI during a naturalistic movie-viewing task depicting social interactions (meets I3) and includes a healthy adult control group (meets I4). However, the NeuroStore record only reports a whole-brain between-group contrast (NT > ASD) and does not report an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain task effect/map for the healthy (NT) group alone. Therefore it fails to provide the required healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked map (I5 not met) and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrast without a healthy-group whole-brain task effect). No evidence in the provided record indicates within-group NT whole-brain results. fulltext_incomplete is false.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (biological motion perception). A healthy adult group is included (n=17, mean age 27.7, within 18–65) and group-level, whole-brain, within-group contrasts for the healthy/control group are reported (e.g., BM > ST; inference over whole brain, FDR q<0.05, peak coordinates in tables). Results are presented as whole-brain voxelwise maps/peaks rather than ROI-only. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study reports an empathy-for-pain fMRI task contrasting painful vs neutral scenarios from self/loved-one/stranger perspectives (social-affiliation/attachment construct). Participants are healthy adults (n=36, mean age 23). Multiple analyses report whole-brain, group-level task-evoked results (e.g., Loved-one pain vs neutral: model fit over whole brain; Pain>Neutral: whole-brain inference with FDR threshold, Table tbl1). Coordinates/peaks are provided. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical data present).

This study uses fMRI with a social task (facial emotion recognition) and includes healthy adult controls (I3 met). However, the NeuroStore record only reports combined-sample whole-brain searchlight results; it does not present a group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Therefore I4 (results for healthy group reported separately) and I5 (healthy-group whole-brain evidence) are not satisfied. No exclusion criteria from the list (E2–E6) are explicitly triggered, but the study fails to meet required inclusion criteria. Based solely on the provided document, the paper must be excluded because it does not provide an unambiguous whole-brain healthy-group map required by the review.

The study tests perception of social signals (audiovisual voices and faces), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The sample is healthy adults (n=24, mean age 26.6), meeting the age/sample criterion. NeuroStore indicates the second-level random-effects model was fit over the whole brain and reported peaks (Table), and thresholding notes an uncorrected conjunction map as well as small-volume correction within ROIs; thus at least one group-level whole-brain voxelwise task analysis/model fit and reported coordinates are available (acceptable per I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, healthy adults reported separately). Therefore the study should be included.

The study reports task-based fMRI of a social cognitive emotion-regulation paradigm (a psychotherapist instructing participants), directly addressing social-related processing. Participants are healthy adults (n=19; ages 22–32), meeting the sample criterion. Multiple group-level, within-subject whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Social-Reg > Social-Look; model fit over: whole brain) are reported with thresholding and peak tables, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, healthy-group task activation maps. Results are reported as tables of peaks and whole-brain contrasts. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text appears complete for screening.
