The study reports task-based fMRI during social decision-making (Prisoner’s Dilemma and Ultimatum Game), recruiting healthy participant groups (Pilot N=10; Main N=15) and presenting group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts with thresholding and reported peak coordinates/tables. These satisfy the review objective and inclusion requirements: I3 (fMRI during social-related tasks), I5 (whole-brain, group-level task activation maps reported), and I6 (results reported as peak tables). The paper also reports healthy adult samples (I4) though exact ages are not listed in the extracted record; participants are described as healthy and no clinical groups are mixed into the reported contrasts, so the healthy-group results are clearly identifiable. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Confidence is reduced slightly because the extraction does not explicitly state participants’ ages, but the documentation clearly indicates healthy adult groups and appropriate whole-brain analyses.

The study reports task-based fMRI measuring responses to faces (socially relevant stimuli) and explicitly investigates facial color processing (a social communication/perception construct). Participants: n=25 healthy adults (mean age 25.24, within 18–65). The paper provides a group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrast (natural-colored face vs scrambled image) with voxel-level thresholding (p<0.001) and reported peak coordinates (Table), fulfilling whole-brain evidence. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, age within range, empirical fMRI data). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6).

The study uses fMRI during a social-related humor appreciation task (meets I3) in a healthy adult sample age 20–30 (meets I4). However, all reported task-evoked activation contrasts were modeled and inferred within regions-of-interest (ROI) with small-volume correction (no unmasked, whole-brain task activation maps). Although the paper reports seed-based PPI connectivity analyses fit over the whole brain, these are connectivity results rather than group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps. Therefore the study does not report the required whole-brain task activation map (fails I5) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI task analyses reported).

Exclusion due to E2: the NeuroStore record indicates analyses were conducted and reported only within a region-of-interest (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest) with no whole-brain, voxelwise healthy-group task activation maps. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task involves social processing — gaze stimuli/social-cognitive context) and I4 (the study includes a healthy neurotypical control group reported in the abstract). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no group-level whole-brain healthy/control task-evoked map is reported). Therefore the study must be excluded for failing to provide whole-brain healthy-group activation required by the review.

The study is excluded because it does not report any whole-brain (voxelwise) healthy-group task activation maps. All reported analyses were fit and inference-restricted to predefined regions of interest with small-volume FWE correction. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related gaze task) and I4 (a healthy control group is reported separately). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain group-level healthy/control voxelwise results are reported). Exclusion criteria met: E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). The NeuroStore record is sufficiently detailed to make this determination; full text appears available in the record.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (movie-based Theory of Mind task; fMRI adaptation of the MASC) in healthy adult participants (n=18, ages 20–45). Multiple group-level, within-group contrasts (ToM > physical inference) were estimated with models fit over the whole brain and inference performed over the whole brain (reported thresholding and cluster criteria), and peak coordinates/tables of results are provided. These satisfy whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked reporting. The document also notes acceptable reporting formats (tables of peaks) and includes complementary model-free (T-PICA) components but does not limit reporting to ROIs or only connectivity. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (self-referential encoding and a social attribution/theory-of-mind task), in a healthy adult sample (n=17; mean age 21.5). Group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) analyses are reported (model fit over: whole brain) with reported peak coordinates and voxel-level thresholding (FDR and voxelwise p<0.001) for multiple within-group contrasts (e.g., Self vs Letter, Self>Mother, Mother>Self, Friends>Bumper Cars). Results are clearly identified as coming from the healthy participant group. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

The study examines social processing (political attitudes with IAT; meets I3) in a healthy adult sample aged 21–40 (meets I4). However, although the model was fit over the whole brain, inference was explicitly restricted to regions of interest and all reported results/peaks derive from ROI-restricted inference. There are no clearly reported unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation maps for the healthy group, so inclusion criterion I5 is not met. This meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results). Therefore the study must be excluded.

The study reports an fMRI experiment of social processing (cyber-ball social interaction and face perception), testing learned social roles — satisfying I3. Participants are healthy adults (n=15, mean age 24.1), satisfying I4. NeuroStore extraction documents a group-level, whole-brain searchlight multivariate analysis with inference over the whole brain (FWE-corrected voxel-level results; reported peaks), satisfying I5 and consistent with acceptable reporting (I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age within range, and empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and none of the exclusions.

Meets inclusion criteria: (I3) Task is social-related—biological motion perception/understanding of others (point-light walkers) engaging social processing (STS); (I4) Healthy adult sample reported separately (n=13, mean age 28.2, within 18–65); (I5) Reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrast (canonical > scrambled) with whole-brain model fit and inference, corrected for multiple comparisons; (I6) Whole-brain results reported as peak coordinates/tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical fMRI data). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports fMRI data from a social-related task (empathic decision-making), meeting I3. The sample is healthy adults (n=32, mean age 22.8), meeting I4. The NeuroStore record documents multiple group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task analyses (one-sample GLMs with whole-brain cluster correction and reported peaks/tables), satisfying I5. Results are reported as peaks/tables/coordinates, acceptable under I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not limited to ROIs only, not only connectivity, not between-group-only, and participants are within the 18–65 range. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study tests trustworthiness judgments of faces (social perception of others) using event-related fMRI, satisfying I3. Participants are healthy adults (n=14, ages 18–30), satisfying I4. The NeuroStore extract reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (e.g., Analysis 11850635_analysis_3: untrustworthy > trustworthy faces; model fit over whole brain; voxel-level threshold p<0.001, cluster extent 5), and coordinates/peaks are reported in MNI, satisfying I5 and I6. Although some contrasts used small-volume correction/ROI inference, at least one unmasked whole-brain within-group task effect is clearly reported. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

The study reports event-related fMRI of anger prosody (a social-communication/emotion task), using a healthy adult sample (n=15, mean age 24.4). The NeuroStore record shows multiple group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked contrasts (e.g., AN+NA > NN and attention interactions) estimated with second-level RFX models and voxelwise thresholds, with reported peak coordinates and a Table (tbl1). Whole-brain results are clearly described. Thus it meets social-related task criterion (I3), sample criterion (I4), and whole-brain reporting requirements (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Inclusion is appropriate.

The study reports fMRI task data examining social processing (Theory of Mind triadic/self/other judgments) in a healthy adult sample (n=19, mean age 26.5), satisfying I3 and I4. Multiple group-level, within-subject whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported (e.g., triad > self/other; conjunction triad ∩ self ∩ other) with whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference using FWE-corrected voxelwise thresholds and tables of peak coordinates, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only (E2), not solely connectivity/resting-state (E3) since whole-brain task activation maps are provided, not only between-group contrasts (E4), participant ages are within 18–65 (E5), and this is empirical fMRI data (E6). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and violates none.

This study should be excluded because it does not provide a whole-brain, group-level task activation map for healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — biological motion perception). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no reported healthy adult group results in the NeuroStore extract; all reported analyses are for a single patient, n=1), and I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked statistical map is reported). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (the paper lacks an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). The NeuroStore record shows only patient (n=1) activation and PPI analyses; although controls are mentioned in the abstract, no whole-brain healthy-group maps or separate healthy-group analyses are provided in the extracted results, so the study does not satisfy the meta-analysis sample and whole-brain evidence requirements.

This fMRI study investigates social perception (perception of intentions from approaching animated characters with angry vs. happy expressions), meeting the review objective. It reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts (Angry>Happy and Happy>Angry) with reported peaks (MNI), model fit over whole brain, and random-effects analysis in a healthy participant sample (n=10). All required whole-brain task-evoked results for the healthy group are present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, participants are described as healthy adults, and the paper is empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This fMRI study used a social decision-making task (Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy adult participants (n=20, ages 23–38). The NeuroStore record reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., Competitive > Cooperative, conjunction) with inference performed over the whole brain and tables of peak coordinates, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Reporting meets acceptable formats (tables). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, empirical fMRI data present).

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (ages 20–26), using a social vs non-social free-recall paradigm (live video of experimenter reactions) addressing social/self-related processing. Whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses are reported (model fit and inference over whole brain) with thresholded results presented as peak coordinates/tables for contrasts including social > non-social. This meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adults 18–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked results), and I6 (coordinates/tables acceptable). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an fMRI study of social communication processing (voice communicative vs noncommunicative), using a Sound/Voice categorization task targeting communicative vocalizations—thus addressing the review objective. The sample is healthy adults (n=20, mean age 22), satisfying the age/sample criterion. The paper reports a within-group whole-brain voxelwise contrast (communicative > noncommunicative) with model fit and inference over the whole brain and voxel-level FDR thresholding, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 18–65, and it is empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 (and I6 as reporting format is acceptable).

NeuroStore extraction indicates fMRI of social cognition (action observation with mentalizing and mirror systems) in healthy adults (n=18, ages 18–32), so inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are satisfied. However, all reported analyses list 'Model fit over: region of interest' and 'Inference restricted to: region of interest' using a mask of the mirror neuron and mentalizing systems; no whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation maps are reported. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence) is NOT met. This study reports only ROI-masked analyses and meets exclusion criterion E2 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete in the provided document (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study reports an fMRI humor-processing task (viewing nonverbal cartoons), which falls under social communication (I3). Participants are reported as 10 healthy participants (all male) and results are reported for this healthy group (I4) though ages are not explicitly listed in the document. The analyses include whole-brain, voxelwise cross-subject regression (model fit over whole brain) with reported Talairach coordinates for significant peaks, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain group-level task-evoked results (I5). Results are reported as coordinates/tables (acceptable per I6). No exclusion criteria are met: this is not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity/resting-state only (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E4), and not a non-empirical paper (E6).

The study is excluded because it does not meet inclusion criterion I3: the task is affective picture matching of threat/non-face images (dogs, sharks, snakes, spiders, guns, car accidents, plane crashes, explosions) and does not constitute a social-related task targeting social constructs (e.g., perception/understanding of others, affiliation, social communication). Although the abstract frames findings in terms of empathy, the reported task/stimuli are non-social threat scenes. The study does meet I4 (healthy adult group reported separately) and I5/I6 (a whole-brain, group-level healthy-control task activation map is reported and thresholded). No exclusion criteria from E2–E6 are directly met. Therefore excluded because I3 is not satisfied.

The study uses fMRI during a social-related task (perception/understanding of self and others: own vs other body perception), includes healthy adult participants (n=15 female, n=15 male; ages within 18–65), and reports multiple group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts for the healthy groups (e.g., own body > scrambled for females and males; whole-brain inference and coordinates/tables provided). Thus it meets I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper).

The study uses fMRI during a social (Theory of Mind/mentalizing) task and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, all reported task analyses were performed and inferred within predefined ROIs (Model fit over: region of interest; Inference restricted to: region of interest; small-volume FWE correction across ROIs). No group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation maps for the healthy/control group are reported in the extracted record, so it fails I5. This meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results). Participants are adults in the 18–65 range. Therefore the paper is excluded because it reports only ROI-based task results and lacks whole-brain healthy-group task maps (E2).

Exclusion E4 met: the paper reports only between-group interactions (responder vs non-responder; medicated vs unmedicated) as whole-brain contrasts and does not present an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map or main effect/within-group contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task: autobiographical recall of emotions — relevant to perception/understanding of self) and I4 (sample: healthy adult participants, n=16, mean age 30.7 within 18–65). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain group-level task-evoked map clearly identified as a healthy/control-group main effect or within-group contrast). I6 is not effectively satisfied because, although coordinates are reported, they pertain only to between-group interactions and not to an unmasked healthy-group whole-brain effect required by I5. Therefore the study must be excluded per E4.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social interaction processing in a healthy participant sample and provides whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: (I3) task is social cognition observing cooperative and affective social interactions; (I4) sample consists of a healthy adult participant group (n=27; sex breakdown reported); (I5) multiple group-level whole-brain within-group contrasts are reported with inference over the whole brain (e.g., cooperative > landscape, affective > landscape, cooperative > affective); (I6) results are reported as coordinate tables/peaks. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and include within-group whole-brain activation maps. The document does not report participant ages explicitly, but it clearly describes a healthy adult sample (n=27) and reports standard whole-brain group effects, satisfying the meta-analysis requirements.

The study uses task fMRI of social perception and includes a healthy adult group, but the NeuroStore record only reports between-group interaction contrasts (HC>SZ and SZ>HC) and does not provide any unmasked, whole-brain group-level healthy-control task activation map or within-group contrast for the healthy participants. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4. Included criteria met: I3 (social-related fMRI task) and I4 (healthy adult group present). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task map reported). No evidence the full text was incomplete.

The study investigates attribution of agency from animated shapes (social perception/understanding of others), meeting the social-related task requirement. Participants are healthy adults (n=12, mean age 25.2), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (High>Low and Low>High) with reported peak coordinates and whole-brain model fitting, satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, outside age range, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and the study should be included.

The study used fMRI during a social task (Cyberball social exclusion/support) in adult undergraduates, reporting whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (Exclusion>Inclusion; Support>Exclusion) with tables of peak coordinates and whole-brain inference. The sample comprises adults (mean age 19.85) and results are reported for the overall participant group rather than only a clinical subgroup. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), and I6 (coordinates reported). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/resting-state only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Note: NeuroStore metadata lists possible comorbidity (social phobia), but the abstract and reported analyses present whole-group results across undergraduates with a range of social anxiety scores rather than only a patient subgroup, supporting inclusion.

Excluded because the paper does not report a separate healthy adult (control) group whole-brain task map. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (no unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect reported). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during social-related task: social reward/being liked) and I6 (whole-brain results are reported in tables/figures). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no clearly reported healthy adult group analyzed separately; sample is mixed and includes participants with current MDD/GAD/social phobia) and I5 (no whole-brain group-level task map clearly identified as coming from a healthy/control group). Full text was available in the NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study used task fMRI during a social decision task (charitable donation), meeting I3. Participants are healthy adults (n=19, mean age 28.2), meeting I4. The NeuroStore record reports within-group, cross-subject regression analyses with reported peaks (group-level reported coordinates), indicating whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results for the healthy group, satisfying I5; the presence of reported peaks (coordinate reporting) also satisfies I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, and empirical fMRI data present). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusions are triggered.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI probing a social/affiliation-related construct (implicit personal space) (I3); the sample is healthy adults within 18–65 (n=22, ages 19–30) (I4); the paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts for the healthy group (e.g., social-chair > non-social-table) with reported peak tables (I5); reporting via tables/peaks satisfies acceptable reporting (I6). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity-only, not only between-group contrasts, age range is appropriate, and the paper is empirical. Full text appears complete for screening.

The NeuroStore record shows fMRI during a social-cognition evaluation task (I3 met). However, the extracted analyses are region-of-interest only ("Model fit over: region of interest"; "Inference restricted to: region of interest"; region-level thresholding), and no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked maps for the healthy group are reported. Therefore this study reports ROI-only results and does not provide qualifying whole-brain evidence, so exclusion criterion E2 applies. Also, the document does not explicitly report the sample as healthy adults aged 18–65 (I4 not confirmed) and does not satisfy I5 (whole-brain evidence). Decision: EXCLUDED based on E2. Inclusion criteria met: I3. Inclusion criteria not met: I4, I5.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It uses task-based fMRI during a social-related facial emotion recognition task (alexithymia and labeling of others’ emotional expressions) — satisfies I3. The sample comprises a healthy adult group (n=50; ages 18–29) reported separately — satisfies I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., HA>NE, AN>NE, FE>NE; second-level whole-brain models and reported peaks) clearly from the healthy group — satisfies I5. Reporting of whole-brain results in tables/peaks is acceptable — satisfies I6. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes within-group whole-brain effects, appropriate age range, and is empirical). Therefore include.

This study reports task-based fMRI of social-related processing (retrieval of person knowledge, social status and personality trait judgments) in healthy adult participants (ages ~20–23; n=24 and n=26 across studies). Multiple analyses report group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked contrasts and corrected inference with reported peak coordinates/tables (e.g., Analyses 21–25 and others), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only without whole-brain task maps, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met.

The study used task-based fMRI to examine learning about other people’s preferences (a social cognition paradigm), meeting I3. The sample is healthy adults (n=25, mean age 25.1), meeting I4. Multiple analyses state ‘Model fit over: whole brain’ and ‘Inference over: whole brain’, with cluster-corrected whole-brain results and reported peak coordinates (MNI), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, outside age range, or non-empirical). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 are met and the paper should be included.

This study reports task-evoked fMRI BOLD responses during a political belief judgment task that probes social-cognitive processing (self/other and social decision-making). Participants are healthy adults (n=26, age range 22–45), satisfying the sample criterion. Analyses are second-level random-effects GLMs fit over the whole brain with whole-brain inference and reported voxelwise peaks (Table 1), meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement; results are coordinate-based and clearly described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants in age range, empirical data present). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related face-processing task (emotional expressions), satisfying I3. The sample consists of healthy adults (n=35, mean age 29), satisfying I4. Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses are reported (whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference; random-effects ANCOVA) including within-group contrasts such as main effect of emotion and angry>neutral/happy, satisfying I5. Results are reported as peak coordinates in tables (acceptable per I6). Thresholding (FDR voxel-level p<0.05) and Talairach coordinates are provided. No exclusion criteria apply: this is not ROI-only (E2), not connectivity/resting-state only (E3), not only between-group contrasts (E4), participants are within 18–65 (E5), and it is an empirical fMRI study (not E6). Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

This study reports fMRI during a social-relevant face perception task (emotional and neutral faces; one-back face identity), satisfying I3. A healthy adult group (n=7, mean age 30) is reported separately, satisfying I4. The paper provides a whole-brain, group-level within-group contrast for healthy controls (rest > faces) with model fit over the whole brain and reported peak coordinates (Table), satisfying I5 and acceptable under I6. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not solely connectivity or resting-state, and include an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective.

This study uses fMRI during a social decision-making task (Ultimatum Game) with healthy adult participants (I3 and I4 met). However, it does not report any group-level, whole-brain within-group (healthy-group) task-evoked activation map. The reported whole-brain analyses are between-group contrasts/interactions (Analyses 0 and 5) rather than unmasked healthy-group main effects, and the within-group effects are reported as ROI analyses (septal region, DLPFC). Connectivity/PPI results are reported separately and do not substitute for a task activation map. Therefore Exclusion criterion E4 applies (only between-group contrasts/interactions reported without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criterion not met: I5. fulltext_incomplete=false

Excluded because the study’s healthy-control group consists of adolescents (TD: mean age 12.23, range 8.32–15.0) and the clinical group is also under 18 (ASD: mean 13.19, range 9.37–17.85). No healthy adult (age 18–65) subgroup is reported. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social-related fMRI task: self/other face recognition), I5 (whole-brain, group-level within-group healthy-control contrasts reported), I6 (results reported as peaks in a table). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (no healthy adult sample 18–65). Exclusion criterion met: E5 (participants only outside 18–65 with no adult subgroup). Therefore the study is excluded from the review.

The task is social (Empathy for Pain), and a healthy adult control group is reported (n=19, ages 33–42), so I3 and I4 are met. However, while the model was fit over the whole brain, inference was explicitly restricted to a region of interest and thresholding used an FDR small-volume correction. This indicates the paper reports only ROI-constrained inference rather than an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map, so it fails I5 and meets exclusion E2 (only ROI analyses/no whole-brain results). Reported peaks likely reflect the ROI-restricted inference and cannot be treated as whole-brain, voxelwise healthy-group results. Therefore the study is excluded.

The study used task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=12, mean age 33.09), meeting the sample criterion. The task involved rating brands, and the authors specifically report contrasts based on a ‘‘social competence’’ factor (brands loading high on social competence) with medial prefrontal cortex activation interpreted as social cognition involvement, indicating the task/analyses probe social-related processing. Whole-brain random-effects analyses were conducted (model fit over: whole brain) and group-level voxelwise contrasts are reported (peaks listed), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirements (reported voxelwise results). Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not between-group-only, ages within 18–65, and it is empirical).

The study reports task-based fMRI during social tasks (face-viewing to track sociometric popularity; Social Evaluative Feedback Task), includes a healthy participant group (14 female, 12 male), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (Analyses 1 and 2: model fit over whole brain; corrected threshold P < 0.05; reported peaks). These meet the review’s requirements for social-related fMRI in healthy adults and whole-brain evidence. The NeuroStore record does not list participant ages explicitly, but the sample is described as healthy participants and is presented as a single healthy/control group; therefore I4 is considered satisfied. No exclusion criteria are met.

Excluded because the paper reports a whole-brain between-group contrast (OXT > PLC) during the Cyberball social task but does not report an unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect (e.g., main effect or within-group task activation). Exclusion criterion met: E4 (reports only a between-group contrast without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — Cyberball Social Exclusion) and I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 18–27). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no clear whole-brain group-level task-evoked map from the healthy/control group independent of the between-group treatment contrast). Full text appears complete for screening.

The study reports task-based fMRI during an evaluative/valence judgment task involving perception of facial and vocal emotional expressions (social communication/perception of others), meeting I3. Participants are healthy adults (n=25; ages 19–24), meeting I4. NeuroStore extraction shows group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (model fit over whole brain, inference over whole brain) with reported peaks/tables for main effects and interaction, meeting I5 and acceptable reporting per I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within 18–65, and empirical fMRI data reported).

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) The study used task-based fMRI of a social interaction (initiating/responding to joint attention with live video face-to-face interaction); (I4) Sample includes healthy adults (n=32, mean age 24.5, within 18–65); (I5) Reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task activation contrasts (multiple within-group contrasts with model fit and inference over whole brain and peak coordinates in tables); (I6) Whole-brain results are reported in tables of coordinates. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and it is empirical).

The study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses fMRI during a social-related face processing task involving affiliation-relevant emotions (I3), reports data from a healthy adult sample (n=40, mean age 29.5) within 18–65 (I4), and includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (Analyses 27856343_analysis_2, _3, and _4 are modeled and inferred over the whole brain), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5). The document also allows whole-brain results reported in the extracted analyses (I6). Although some analyses are ROI-restricted (Analyses 0 and 1), the presence of whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked group results means the paper is not excluded by ROI-only criteria. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

The study investigates affective speech comprehension (affective classification of sentences), a social-communication/mind-reading task, using fMRI in healthy adults (n=23, mean age 23.3). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (e.g., Analysis 16525130_analysis_4: model fit over whole brain; voxel-level threshold p<0.001; reported peak coordinates/tables), and NeuroStore extraction lists multiple whole-brain contrast peak tables. Results for the healthy sample are clearly the focus. Thus inclusion criteria I3 (social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (coordinate tables acceptable) are met. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are triggered.

Study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) used fMRI during a social processing task (participants viewed human–human and human–robot social interactions and made social judgments), (I4) reports a healthy adult sample (n=26, ages 18–35), (I5) reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and parametric modulations with whole-brain inference (Model fit over: whole brain; Inference over: whole brain; reported peaks/tables), and (I6) whole-brain results are reported as peak coordinates/tables. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, age range appropriate, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition using animations interpreted as social interactions and instructions to attend to social (Behavioral) vs spatial properties (I3). The sample is healthy adults (n=16, mean age 24) (I4). The NeuroStore record reports multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Analyses 18065722_analysis_14, _15, _16: Behavioral vs Spatial and Spatial vs Behavioral with whole-brain FWE-corrected inference reported in Table 3), so whole-brain evidence is present (I5,I6). Although many ROI/SVC analyses are reported, whole-brain results are not restricted to ROIs, so the study is not excluded by the ROI-only criterion. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult volunteers (n=19) performing an evaluative social-emotion task (guilt and embarrassment), addressing social-related processing. Multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts and cross-subject regression analyses are reported with coordinate tables (MNI) and peak reports (guilt>neutral, embarrassment>neutral, embarrassment>guilt, correlations with self-ratings), satisfying whole-brain evidence. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are healthy adults, and the paper is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

The study used task-based fMRI of affective (social) touch (CT-targeted slow brushing), meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample comprises healthy adults (n=22; ages 19–35), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports multiple group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (arm vs baseline, palm vs baseline, arm>palm, palm>arm) with model fit and inference performed over the whole brain (RFX GLM) and peaks reported in tables, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence criterion; tables of coordinates/peaks are provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not exclusively connectivity/resting-state, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical fMRI data present).

This study meets all inclusion criteria: I3—Task is processing vocalizations (social communication), including speech and emotional human sounds; I4—Healthy adult sample reported separately (n=20, ages 20–28); I5—Multiple group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts are reported (model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain; FWE-corrected voxelwise p<0.05); I6—Results include reported peaks/coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, not outside age range, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of social-related fMRI processing in healthy adults.

The study uses task-based fMRI examining human voice versus non-vocal sounds, which falls under social communication/perception of others (I3). The sample is healthy adults (n=13, ages 21–41) meeting the 18–65 requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts (vocal > non-vocal) with reported peak coordinates and voxelwise FDR correction, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/seed connectivity only, not only between-group contrasts, and participants are within age range). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be included.

The study reports an fMRI empathy task (Empathy for Pain) addressing social processing (empathy/perception of others). It includes a healthy adult control group (n=14, mean age 27.2, within 18–65) with results reported separately. Importantly, a group-level whole-brain, within-group contrast for controls is provided (Analysis 25963262_analysis_0: model fit over whole brain, one-sample t-test, whole-brain inference, reported peaks/tables), meeting the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Results are reported with coordinates and cluster thresholds. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes healthy-group whole-brain map, adult ages). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This study investigates social sharing of emotions using fMRI in healthy adults and reports ROI-corrected activations (small-volume FWE) and coordinate tables. However, although the model was fit over the whole brain, inference was explicitly restricted to a region-of-interest (small-volume correction), and no unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map is reported. Therefore it does not meet the requirement for whole-brain evidence (I5) and falls under exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 20–33), and I6 (coordinates/tables reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no clear whole-brain group-level voxelwise task effect reported).

The study tests emotion (including social-affiliative ‘tenderness’) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (ages ~24–26), meeting I3 and I4. It reports group-level, whole-brain task activation contrasts (Analyses 30087646_analysis_5 and _6: whole-brain inference with tables of peaks), satisfying I5 and I6. Results are reported for the healthy sample (n=8) and are not limited solely to ROI analyses or connectivity-only approaches. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the article qualifies for inclusion.

This study reports an event-related fMRI experiment using a social game (the game of Chicken) probing mentalizing and social decision-making (meets I3). Participants are 16 healthy adults (mean age 21.9, in the 18–65 range; meets I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (contrast human > computer) with inference over the whole brain (FDR-corrected P < 0.05, cluster extent reported), i.e., a healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (meets I5 and acceptable reporting per I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Therefore the study should be included.

The study reports task-based fMRI of social/mentalizing processing (Dynamic Interacting Shape Clips; False Belief Task) in a healthy adult sample (n=22; age 18–25). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts for the healthy group are reported (friends>watch; friends>size) with thresholding and tables of peak coordinates. All required inclusion criteria for social fMRI, healthy adult sample, and whole-brain task-evoked maps are satisfied. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met.

This study uses fMRI during a social-empathy task (first-person video clips of social-positive, reactive-aggressive, and neutral interactions with instructions to empathize), includes a healthy adult sample (n=20, mean age 24.6), and reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrasts (model fit and inference over whole brain; Talairach coordinates; tables of reported peaks). Thresholding and cluster criteria are provided. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for social-related fMRI in healthy adults and reports whole-brain task activation maps (coordinate tables). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full text appears available via the provided NeuroStore extraction (no access-notice).

This fMRI study examines attribution of intentions to human-made products (mental state attribution), fitting the review’s social processing domain. Participants are healthy adults (n=12, ages 21–31). The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain within-group contrast (Composer > Computer) with model fit and inference over the whole brain and reported peaks (Table 1), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. ROI analyses are present (aMFC correlation) but are supplementary to whole-brain results. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, empirical fMRI data).

The NeuroStore record describes an fMRI study using a social cognition task (videos of cooperative vs noncooperative interaction) with healthy matched controls and patients with schizophrenia, so I3 (social task) and I4 (healthy adult group present) are met. However, the only reported whole-brain analysis in the record is a group-by-condition interaction (between-group omnibus contrast). The record does not report any unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group alone (e.g., main effect or within-group contrast for controls). Therefore the study does not meet I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (reports only between-group contrasts/interaction without a whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria applied: E4. Full text is considered complete for the purposes of this record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

Study uses task-based fMRI examining social-related processing (kinship and moral dilemmas during naturalistic movie viewing and a moral judgment task). Participants are healthy adults (n=30, ages 19–39). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (inter-subject correlation contrasts across the whole brain and a one-sample GLM decision>non-decision contrast) with reported peak coordinates/tables. Thus it meets inclusion criteria for fMRI social tasks in healthy adults and provides whole-brain results in acceptable formats. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not only connectivity/resting-state, includes task activation maps, participants are within age range, and it is empirical).

The study reports an event-related fMRI task examining social perception (violations of social expectations when viewing politicians), satisfying the social-related task requirement. Participants are healthy adults (n=18, ages 19–30), meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports a group-level, whole-brain within-group contrast (Incongruent > Congruent) analyzed with second-level one-sample t-tests; model fit and inference were conducted over the whole brain and peaks are reported (Table), satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, ages within 18–65, and it is empirical).

The study reports task-based fMRI in a social decision-making paradigm (social cognition/games) in healthy adult participants (n=51, mean age 22). It provides group-level, whole-brain within-group contrast results (controlled > free decisions) with whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference and reported peak coordinates, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps. Reporting of peaks/tables satisfies acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within 18–65, empirical data). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

This study used task-based fMRI with social/mentalizing stimuli (listening to literary excerpts with mentalizing vs action content), enrolled healthy adults aged 18–27 (n=18), and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise contrasts (Mentalizing > Action; Action > Mentalizing) with cluster-level inference and reported peak coordinates. The task and contrasts clearly index social cognition/understanding of others. Results are whole-brain and not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only analyses. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

The study reports task-based fMRI during an emotion-regulation task using faces (angry facial expressions), which is a social processing paradigm (perception/understanding of others). The sample consists of healthy adults (n=60, age range 18–57). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Observe-angry > Increase/Decrease and Decrease > Observe-angry) with cluster-level inference and tables of peaks, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Resting-state seed connectivity is also reported but does not preclude inclusion because whole-brain task results are present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Study uses task-based fMRI of social gaze perception (Facial Emotion Recognition Task) addressing social processing (gaze direction and duration) — satisfies I3. Sample is healthy adults (n=22, mean age 27.2) — satisfies I4. Analyses report whole-brain model fit and whole-brain inference with coordinates/peaks reported in tables (voxelwise group-level contrasts and parametric modulation) — satisfies I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply: not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within 18–65, and is empirical fMRI data. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This study reports task-based fMRI of a social interaction paradigm (human-human vs human-machine competition with explicit mentalizing/ToM instructions), satisfying the social-processing requirement. Participants are healthy adults (n=14; mean age 35.9, SD 7.2), meeting the sample criterion. The analyses were performed as whole-brain random-effects GLMs (model fit over whole brain) and the paper reports group-level voxelwise task contrasts with peak coordinates (tables of peaks), satisfying the whole-brain evidence and reporting acceptability criteria. The reported contrasts are within-group effects for the healthy sample. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are in the 18–65 range, and this is empirical fMRI work). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It uses fMRI during a social-related task (emotion regulation in response to dynamic facial expressions; imitation and expressive suppression) satisfying I3. The sample is healthy adults (n=20, mean age 33.5, SD 4.5), satisfying I4. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (second-stage one-sample t-tests) were conducted and reported (model fit over: whole brain; reported coordinate peaks/tables for multiple within-group contrasts), satisfying I5 and I6 (results reported as coordinate tables). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within age range, and this is empirical fMRI data. Therefore the study should be included.

The study investigates perception of direct vs. averted gaze (social cognition—perception/understanding of others) using task-based fMRI in healthy adults (n=24, mean age 30). It reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task contrasts (one-sample t-tests; direct>averted and other within-group contrasts) with peak coordinates (Talairach) and thresholding details. Thus it meets the meta-analysis objective and provides whole-brain healthy-group activation maps.

The study used fMRI during an Emotional Face Matching Task (social perception of others/emotional faces), included a healthy adult sample (n=38, mean age 27.5, screened for psychiatric/neurological disorders), and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise within-group contrast results (FACES > OBJECTS) with whole-brain inference and cluster-level FWE thresholding and a table of 72 reported peaks. These elements satisfy inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=18, ages 18–41) using videos of communicative speech acts (social communication). Group-level random-effects analyses were performed and whole-brain, voxelwise contrasts are reported (e.g., Request > Naming and speech act conditions > face control) with whole-brain inference (FDR voxel-level) and coordinate peaks provided. Thus the paper provides healthy-group, whole-brain task-evoked activation maps for a social-related task and meets the review’s reporting allowance for tables/coordinates. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and it is empirical).

The study uses task fMRI of a social task (Ultimatum Game), and includes a healthy adult control group (I3 and I4 met). However, all reported statistical maps in the NeuroStore record appear to be between-group contrasts or interactions (controls vs. depressed; depressed vs. controls). The record does not report any unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group alone (no within-group or main-effect healthy-control whole-brain results are provided). Therefore exclusion criterion E4 applies (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect). fulltext_incomplete=false.

This study reports fMRI BOLD data collected during a social cognition task (False Belief/ToM animations), includes a healthy adult sample with ages 24–64 (within 18–65), and provides a group-level, whole-brain within-group contrast (ToM > R) with whole-brain model fitting and inference (FWE-thresholded results and reported peak coordinates). Thus it meets the review’s requirements for task, sample, and whole-brain healthy-group activation maps. No exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI during social contexts (cooperative, competitive, and individual conditions with empathic stimuli) addressing social cognition/empathy (I3); reports results from a healthy adult sample (n=16, mean age 23.2) (I4); and provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts and coordinate peaks for multiple within-group contrasts (e.g., cooperation > competition, cooperation > individual, pain contrasts) fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements (I5). Reporting includes tables of peaks/coordinates (acceptable per I6). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical fMRI data present).

The study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (mentalizing; judging others’ preferences) in healthy adults (n=64, ages 18–26), satisfying I3 and I4. The NeuroStore record specifies whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with inference over the whole brain (Analyses 20534459_analysis_0 and _2), meeting I5. The report format and coordinate space are provided (MNI), and whole-brain results/peaks are reported, consistent with I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adults within 18–65, and is empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) Task is social-related (viewing social-communicative actions such as waving); (I4) Sample consists of healthy adults (n=36, ages 18–28 reported); (I5) Reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation maps (SA>MA and MA>SA contrasts; model fit and inference over whole brain with FWE correction); (I6) Results are reported (peaks/tables). No exclusion criteria are met: not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, participants within age range, and is empirical. Therefore the study should be included for the review of social-related fMRI in healthy adults.

The study reports task-based fMRI during an explicitly social language/communication task (hyperscanning verbal interaction) in healthy adults (n=38; ages 21–36). It includes group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise second-level analyses (one-sample random-effects t-test and parametric modulation) with inference reported across the whole brain (FWE cluster-level thresholding) and coordinates/tables of peaks. Thus I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task maps), and I6 (acceptable reporting formats) are satisfied. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical fMRI data present).

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. It used task-based fMRI (BOLD) during a social-related attribution task probing self-responsibility/self-serving bias (I3). The sample includes a healthy adult group (n=12, age range 20–51, mean 34) satisfying the 18–65 requirement (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with voxel-level correction for multiple comparisons and tables of reported peak coordinates for within-group contrasts (internal>external, external>internal, self-serving, non-self-serving), thus providing whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, and participants are within the eligible age range. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study reports task-based fMRI of a social-related construct (empathy for others' pain) and includes a healthy adult control group (n=13, mean age 33). It provides group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps for the healthy/control group (Control: Painful > Nonpainful; FDR-corrected p < 0.05 voxel-level; reported peaks/tables). Results for the healthy group are reported separately (within-group contrasts and regressions). Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. NeuroStore record represents the article’s reported whole-brain results for the control group, enabling inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The study used fMRI of guilt-related autobiographical and hypothetical scenarios in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4). NeuroStore reports voxelwise model estimation over the whole brain but inference was explicitly restricted to predefined regions with FWE small-volume correction (SVC) and reported peaks within ROI masks; no unmasked whole-brain group-level task activation map is reported. Therefore it does not meet I5 (whole-brain evidence) and effectively reports only ROI-constrained inference, which triggers exclusion E2. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I6 (coordinates reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no unmasked whole-brain group-level map). Exclusion criteria met: E2 (only ROI analyses reported).

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria. I3: The paradigm includes social feedback (an avatar that gradually smiles), which engages social-related processing (perception of social reward/social cues). I4: The sample comprises healthy adult participants (n=24, mean age 24.75, within 18–65). I5: The paper reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked results (Analyses labeled to run inference over whole brain with FWE correction and reported peak coordinates/Tables t1–t3). I6: Whole-brain results are reported in tables of coordinates (reported peaks) and described in analyses. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are provided. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study meets the meta-analysis objective and all required inclusion criteria. It uses task-based fMRI of social processing (reasoning about others’ facial expressions/empathy), fulfilling I3. The sample is 26 healthy adults with ages 22–61, within 18–65, fulfilling I4. The report includes group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (e.g., face > scrambled; reasoning contrasts) with inference over the whole brain and tables of peak coordinates, fulfilling I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, and healthy-group whole-brain task effects are explicitly reported. Therefore the paper should be INCLUDED.

The study used fMRI during a social judgment task and included healthy adult control participants (meets I3 and I4). However, the NeuroStore extract only reports between-group interaction contrasts (e.g., controls vs ASD; SPD vs ASD) and some ROI eigenvariate analyses. There is no reported unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (i.e., no whole-brain within-group healthy social task effect). This violates inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts/ROI results without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Therefore the study is excluded.

This study is excluded because it does not meet the social-task inclusion criterion (I3). While the abstract frames event simulation as relevant to social cognition generally, the experimental task used object-picture sets (three-object arrays) and required matching object names or situation descriptions and predicting subsequent situation — there is no clear evidence the task probed social processes (e.g., perception/understanding of others, mentalizing) or used social stimuli/agents. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (healthy adult sample, n=20, mean age 20.65 within 18–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise contrasts reported), and I6 (whole-brain results reported as peak coordinates/tables). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (study does not clearly use a social-related task). Exclusion criteria met: none []. Full text is complete as provided (fulltext_incomplete=false).

The study investigates mental simulation of self-motion (egocentric mental rotation), which falls under ‘Perception and Understanding of Self’ (I3). Participants are healthy adults (n=20, ages 20–40), meeting the sample inclusion (I4). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level within-subject contrasts for healthy participants (e.g., no rotation GVS > no rotation sham; GVS > sham overall) with voxelwise FWE-corrected results (Analyses 3 and 4), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5) and acceptable reporting formats (I6). Multiple ROI analyses are also present, but they do not preclude inclusion because qualifying whole-brain results are reported. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study meets the review objective and all required inclusion criteria. I3: The task is explicitly social (group membership, perception of others’ actions) and was scanned with fMRI. I4: Participants are healthy adults (group-level samples reported; mean age 23.8, range includes 17–43 but the sample is described as healthy participants and includes adults within 18–65). I5/I6: The paper reports multiple group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., own team > other team; team actions > baseline; judgment vs passive viewing) with whole-brain inference and reported peaks/coordinates. Although one analysis used an ROI, whole-brain group maps are present. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears available in the study document, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study uses task-based fMRI of a social interactive reactive aggression paradigm (social processing). The sample comprises healthy adults (n=14, mean age 28.6), meeting the age and health requirements. Multiple analyses report group-level, whole-brain, within-group task contrasts and parametric modulations with whole-brain inference and FDR voxelwise thresholding (Analyses 2, 4, 5, 6) with reported peak tables, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps. Thus inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (e.g., results are not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, and include unmasked healthy-group whole-brain effects).

This fMRI study investigates recognition of basic facial expressions (social communication / perception of others) using visual and haptic tasks, satisfying the review’s social-related construct. It includes a healthy adult sighted group (n=22, mean age 36.5) reported separately, meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level within-group task contrasts for the sighted healthy group (e.g., VFE > VS and HFE > HS) with peaks/tables in MNI space (cluster-corrected inference), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement; coordinate tables/peaks are provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, contains unmasked healthy-group whole-brain task effects).

The NeuroStore record indicates this is an fMRI study of social gaze (meets I3) with a healthy adult control group reported separately (n=16; meets I4). However, the only extracted group-level result for healthy controls is a region-of-interest analysis: 'Model fit over: region of interest' and 'Inference restricted to: region of interest' with SVC. No whole-brain (voxelwise) healthy-group task activation map is reported in the document. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only results). Full text is available as the NeuroStore-derived record (fulltext_incomplete=false).

This study meets all inclusion criteria. It uses fMRI during a social-related task (perception/classification of different laughter types; social communication/perception of others) (I3). The sample is healthy adults (n=18, mean age 26, 9F/9M) within 18–65 (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise random-effects task contrasts (multiple within-group contrasts; model fit and inference over whole brain) and peak coordinates in tables (I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not between-group-only). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

The study used fMRI during a clearly social task (viewing/responding to social vignettes) with BOLD measures and an event-related design, satisfying I3. The sample is healthy adults (n=21; ages 18–34), satisfying I4. The NeuroStore extraction indicates model fit and inference were performed over the whole brain and reports group-level within-group contrasts with coordinate tables (Table t1), satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports healthy-group whole-brain task activations).

The study reports task-based fMRI (BOLD) during a social-related Free Recall Task focused on relationship episodes (meets I3). The sample is healthy adults (n=35, mean age 33.85, within 18–65) with diagnostic screening (meets I4). The NeuroStore extract indicates whole-brain model fitting and whole-brain inference for within-group contrasts (self-relevant > control; other > control) with reported peak coordinates/tables (meets I5 and I6). Thresholding and random-effects GLM are described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants in range, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This study uses fMRI during a social-related task (social reward in an incentive delay task), includes a healthy adult sample within 18–65 (n=63, ages 20.4–29.1), and reports a group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task activation map (Analysis 25944965_analysis_0: reward cues > neutral cues; whole-brain model and inference; voxel-level FWE). Whole-brain peaks are reported, satisfying the review’s requirement for voxelwise healthy-group task effects. Although several analyses use ROIs, the presence of an unmasked whole-brain group contrast fulfills inclusion criteria.

Excluded because the paper reports only ROI-restricted inference / small-volume-corrected results and ROI-only analyses; no unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy group is reported. Exclusion criteria met: E2. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI face-processing social task) and I4 (healthy adult sample, mean age 25.6). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain, voxelwise healthy-group task-evoked statistical map reported). Analyses either fit models over ROIs or performed whole-brain model fitting with inference restricted to ROIs (SVC), which amounts to ROI-restricted results rather than unmasked whole-brain results.

This fMRI study examines emotion processing and mirror-neuron-related responses using an affective picture viewing task (IAPS) tied to trained visuomotor associations, which pertains to social-related processing (perception/understanding of others/emotion), satisfying I3. The sample is healthy adults (n=19, mean age 27.7) within 18–65, satisfying I4. Multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses/contrasts are reported (model fit over whole brain and inference over whole brain for training and emotion contrasts; reported coordinates and peaks), satisfying I5 and I6. The report includes whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (coordinate tables, cluster-level FWE thresholding) rather than ROI-only or connectivity-only results. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This fMRI study uses a social cognition task (empathy, Theory of Mind, self-other differentiation) with task-evoked BOLD responses, meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample is a healthy adult group (n=15, ages 21–40), meeting the sample criterion. The NeuroStore extraction shows group-level, whole-brain voxelwise model fits and within-group contrasts (model fit over: whole brain; inference over whole brain for interaction contrasts) with reported coordinate peaks, satisfying whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore the paper should be included.

The study collected fMRI BOLD data from healthy adult participants (n=34, mean age 21.8) performing a social evaluation task (liking/disliking images of people), satisfying I3 and I4. The NeuroStore record reports multiple group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked analyses (whole-brain model fit and inference, 2×2 ANOVA and contrasts like Homeless>Control, main effects, and interactions) with reported peak coordinates/tables, satisfying I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, and include whole-brain healthy-group task effects rather than only between-group contrasts. Therefore the paper meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This study reports task-based fMRI in a social gaze paradigm (social-related processing). Participants are healthy adults (n=23, age range 21–37). The NeuroStore record indicates a group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analysis (model fit over: whole brain; inference over: whole brain) for the contrast INC_SOC > CON_SOC (one-sample t-test with RT covariate), with reported peaks and cluster-level correction. Thus it provides an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map meeting the review’s whole-brain evidence requirement. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply.

The study uses an emotion (facial expression) task, so it meets I3 (social-related task). However, the participant sample reported is 'patients' with Autism Spectrum Disorder, age mean 14.56 (range 12.01–18.53), i.e. adolescents only; no healthy adult (age 18–65) group results are reported separately. Therefore inclusion criteria I4 (healthy adult sample) and I5 (whole-brain task map from a healthy/control group) are not met. This violates exclusion criterion E5 (participants outside 18–65 with no eligible healthy adult subgroup). Although whole-brain within-group contrasts are reported, they pertain to a patient adolescent sample rather than healthy adults, so the study is excluded.

The study reports an fMRI verbal politeness judgment task addressing social communication (verbal politeness), meeting the review objective. Participants are 20 healthy adults (no neurological/psychiatric history reported), satisfying the sample criterion. Group-level SPM whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported (multiple within-group contrasts, peaks/tables provided) with whole-brain inference, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements; results are reported as coordinate peaks/tables which is acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within adult range, and it is empirical fMRI data). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria are triggered.

Exclusion E4: The paper does not report an unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map for the healthy/control group alone. While the study used fMRI during a social-related task (mirror neuron / perception of others) and includes a non-ALEX (healthy) adult group (I3 and I4 met), the only whole-brain result reported in the NeuroStore record is a conjunction analysis across both groups (a conjunction of two one-sample tests) and the between-group/interaction contrasts were tested only within an ROI. No standalone, voxelwise healthy-group (control) task map is clearly reported; therefore it fails I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4.

This study meets the review objective and all inclusion criteria. It uses fMRI during a social-related Emotional Face Matching Task (I3). The sample comprises healthy adults (n=20, ages 18–43) (I4). Crucially, the paper reports a group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task analysis: Analysis 22832391_analysis_0 is a drug x sociality x familiarity interaction with model fit and inference over the whole brain and whole-brain FWE correction, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement (I5). Results are clearly from the healthy participant group. I6 (acceptability of reporting location) is also satisfied. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. The study should therefore be included.

The study reports whole-brain task-evoked fMRI results of gesture/speech narrative processing (a social communication task) in healthy adults (n=20, ages 22–35). NeuroStore extract shows model fit and inference over the whole brain, voxelwise contrasts and reported peak coordinates, satisfying whole-brain reporting. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported), I5 (whole-brain group-level voxelwise results), and I6 (results described and reported). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

Excluded (E4) because the paper does not report any whole-brain, group-level task activation map clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. Inclusion met: I3 (study uses fMRI during a social-cognition task). Inclusion not met: I4 (although a healthy control group exists, results for the healthy group are not reported separately as a group-level whole-brain map) and I5 (no whole-brain healthy-group task effect is presented; reported whole-brain maps are for all subjects combined and between-group contrasts). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (the reported results rely on combined-subject maps and between-group contrasts without an accompanying unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group activation map). Full text was sufficiently represented in the provided NeuroStore record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study investigates social-related processing (empathy for pain; manipulation of social context and perceived agency), uses fMRI, and reports results from healthy adult participants (n=26; mean age 24.4). Importantly, the paper includes multiple group-level, whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., Pain>no pain; pain x social context interaction) with whole-brain inference and voxelwise FDR thresholding, and reports peak coordinates/tables. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria apply.

The study uses task-based fMRI of social cognition (false-belief/Theory-of-Mind cartoons) in healthy adult participants (n=13, ages 22–38), satisfying I3 and I4. However, all reported group-level analyses are described as region-of-interest (model fit over: region of interest; inference restricted to: region of interest) and a MARSBAR ROI analysis is noted; no unmasked, whole-brain voxelwise group-level task activation map is reported. Therefore the paper does not meet I5 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion E2 (ROI-only results). Reported coordinate peaks appear to come from ROI analyses. Full text is available in the record, so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports task-based fMRI in a social-cognition/legal decision-making paradigm (reading crime vignettes with responsibility/punishment ratings), with healthy adult participants (n=20, ages 18–45). Multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts are reported (e.g., strong disgust > weak disgust; trait > biological), with inference performed over the whole brain and results reported as peak coordinates in tables. Reporting and thresholding (FDR) are appropriate and clearly describe healthy-group task effects. Therefore all inclusion criteria for task relevance, sample, and whole-brain reporting are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The paper reports an fMRI perceptual judgment of self vs non-self body-odour peptides in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4). However, NeuroStore indicates inference was restricted to a region-of-interest despite the model being fit over the whole brain. No unmasked, whole-brain group-level task activation map is reported; results are ROI-restricted. Therefore the study fails I5 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). No other exclusion criteria appear to apply.

The study used task-based fMRI of observation and motor imagery of face and limb movements, which pertains to social-related processing (gesture/face movements relevant to social communication). Participants are healthy adults (mean age 25.18, sd 4.25), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports multiple group-level, whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (model fit over whole brain; inference over whole brain; voxelwise FWE-corrected results) such as within-group contrasts (e.g., limb > face, observation vs imagery), with coordinates/peaks reported. Thus all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

The paper reports fMRI during a social-related False Belief Task (I3) and includes a healthy adult control group (I4). However, NeuroStore extracts show only between-group interaction contrasts (e.g., healthy > ASD, ASD > healthy) and ROI-restricted within-patient analyses; there is no unmasked, whole-brain, group-level healthy-control task activation map reported in the extracted analyses. Therefore the study fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying whole-brain healthy-group task effect).

The study reports task-evoked fMRI (BOLD) during a social task (minimal group membership and emotional face processing), satisfying I3. Participants are healthy adults (n=20, mean age 23.4), satisfying I4. The NeuroStore record indicates model fit and inference were conducted over the whole brain with cluster-level FWE correction and reported peak coordinates/tables, satisfying I5; coordinate/peak reporting also satisfies I6.
