No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, and empirical fMRI data present).

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social provocation/aggression paradigm (Taylor aggression task) involving interaction with an opponent, meeting the review’s social-processing construct. Participants are a healthy adult sample (n=93 males), satisfying the sample criterion. Model fitting and inference were performed over the whole brain with voxelwise, cluster-level FWE-thresholded results and peak coordinates reported in tables, fulfilling the requirement for whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps; results are provided in coordinate tables. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, task effects missing for the healthy group, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

The study reports an fMRI interpersonal pleasant touch task addressing social reward (meets I3). A healthy control group of adults (n=24, age 23.7) is reported separately (meets I4). A within-group whole-brain, voxelwise contrast for controls is provided (Analysis 30658938_analysis_0; model fit over: whole brain; reported peaks), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked results (meets I5). Results are reported as peaks/coordinates (meets I6). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, includes healthy adults, empirical). Full text appears sufficiently represented in the document.

The study meets all inclusion criteria for the review. I3: The task involves perception/understanding of others (identification of deceptive actions and prediction of opponent’s movement), a social-related processing construct. I4: Samples are healthy adult participants (three groups, ages 19–33), reported separately. I5: The paper reports multiple group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked contrasts (within-group deception and direction contrasts for each healthy group; model fit and inference over whole brain; FWE-corrected maps with reported peak coordinates). I6: Whole-brain results are reported as tables of coordinates/peaks. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, include within-group whole-brain effects, participants are within the 18–65 range, and the paper is empirical. The study uses task fMRI with healthy adult participants and includes social-emotional tasks (gender identification of angry and happy faces), satisfying inclusion criteria I3 and I4. However, all reported analyses are region-of-interest (model fit and inference restricted to ROIs) rather than whole-brain voxelwise group-level task maps. Therefore it does not meet inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain evidence) and meets exclusion criterion E2 (studies reporting only ROI analyses with no whole-brain results). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4. Inclusion criteria not met: I5. Exclusion criteria met: E2. The provided NeuroStore record appears complete for screening (fulltext available).

The study meets inclusion criteria: it uses task-based fMRI with an Emotional Face Matching Task (social stimuli) (I3); sample comprises 55 healthy adult participants (mean age 24.9) (I4); it reports a group-level, whole-brain within-group contrast (social > control) with model fit and inference over the whole brain, FWE voxel-level thresholding (Analysis 23554586_analysis_0), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirement (I5). The NeuroStore record reports peaks and other analyses but does not indicate any exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete in the NeuroStore record.

This study reports only group-difference (patient > control) whole-brain connectivity/interaction results during a script-driven anger task; no unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked (within-group or main effect) voxelwise map for the healthy participants is reported in the NeuroStore record. Exclusion IDs met: E3 (connectivity-only results without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation) and E4 (only between-group contrast/interaction reported without an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Inclusion criteria met: I4 (sample includes healthy adult participants age 18–65). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (task is emotion/anger induction but social nature not clearly established in the record), I5 (no healthy-group whole-brain task map reported), and I6 (not applicable because no healthy-group whole-brain results to accept in any reporting form). Based on these, the paper does not meet all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study used task-based fMRI during a social cognition/charitable giving task (meets I3). Participants are healthy adults (n=32, ages 20–34), meeting the age/sample criterion (I4). The paper reports at least one group-level whole-brain, voxelwise within-group contrast (Analysis 27122031_analysis_0: low>high donations; model fit and inference over whole brain with FWE correction), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements (I5). The reported whole-brain result is clearly described (tabulated/extracted peaks), satisfying I6. No exclusion criteria apply: analyses include whole-brain task activation (so E2, E3, E4 do not apply), participants are within 18–65 (E5 not met), and this is an empirical fMRI study (E6 not met).
